name: Tempeh Biryani
intro: Tempeh is my go-to vegan protein and I prefer it to other plant-based meats. Tempeh isn’t made of soya or wheat chunks, but is derived from gut-friendly fermented soya instead. It’s an Indonesian kitchen staple that works perfectly in a biryani instead of meat.

ingredients.item: saffron soaked in 2 tbsp of almond milk

method: In a bowl, mix the vegan cream with the ginger, garlic, biryani masala, garam masala, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder and salt. Whisk well, then add the cubed tempeh, and toss to coat well. Allow it to marinate for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, parboil the rice until it is two-thirds done (about 15 minutes), drain and set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a medium pan over medium heat, and cook the onions until well-browned, for about 20 minutes. Set aside.
Pull out the tempeh cubes (reserving the marinade) and grill them in a grill pan over medium heat for 20 minutes, until crispy on the outside.

In a heavy-bottomed vessel, heat the remaining 3 tbsp of oil over medium heat and add all the whole spices. Once they begin to crackle, add half of the browned onions and sauté for 1 minute. Add the tomato and sauté for 2-3 minutes over a low flame.
Add the reserved marinade and cook for 6-7 minutes. If the mixture is too dry, add a few tablespoons of water.
Add the grilled tempeh to this mixture and stir to coat them in the gravy. Cook for another minute on medium heat then remove them from the vessel.

Layer the pot with the parboiled rice and tempeh. Drizzle with the saffron milk and rose water (if using), and top with the reserved browned onions. Cover the pot with a heavy lid and allow the rice to cook thoroughly, about 5 minutes over a low flame.
Garnish with chopped mint and coriander and serve hot.

name: Tempeh Chickpea Stuffed Mini Peppers
intro: Colorful mini bell peppers wrap these protein-packed appetizers into pretty little packages. Chickpeas and tempeh are just the start of a flavorful mix.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into 1-inch cubes
arge sweet potato, peeled and chopped into bite-size chunks
red bell pepper, chopped into large pieces
yellow bell pepper, chopped into large pieces
Extra virgin olive oil, for grilling
15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
4-ounce can black olives, drained and sliced
chili pepper, such as jalapeño or cayenne, chopped fine
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into 1-inch cubes
seitan, crumbled (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
28-ounce can chickpeas, drained (save the liquid to use as aquafaba) and rinsed
raw almonds, soaked in water from one hour to overnight
extra virgin olive oil, more if desired
seitan, crumbled (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
medium sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped into 2-inch cubes (equal to 2 cups mashed sweet potato)
14-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
tapioca starch or tapioca flour (they are the same thing)
15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
hot chili pepper, sliced thin crosswise
baby spinach, with stems chopped off
seitan (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
tempeh, diced very small, or pulsed small
15-ounce can chickpeas, drained (save the liquid to use as aquafaba) and rinsed

method: Cut off the stem end of the peppers. Slice lengthwise. Remove any seeds that are inside. Set aside.
Place all the remaining ingredients in a food processor. Pulse four or five times. The chickpeas should be chunky. Remove the blade and stir to make sure the mixture is blended well.
Stuff each pepper half full with about 2 tablespoons of the chickpea mixture. Set on a plate to serve.

name: Tempeh Kabobs with Moroccan Couscous
intro: Soaked in a delicious honey-soy marinade and paired with grilled vegetables, these kabobs will please both meat-eaters and vegetarians .

ingredients.item: (8 ounces) of package tempeh, cut into 1/2 inch squares
large red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces

method: Place tempeh, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and cherry tomatoes in a large resealable plastic bag. In a mixing bowl, whisk together olive oil, soy sauce, teriyaki sauce, and honey; season with 1 tablespoon ginger, 1 tablespoon garlic, and salt and pepper to taste. Pour mixture over tempeh and veggies, seal, and shake to coat. Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Preheat grill for medium-high heat. Thread tempeh and veggies on skewers. Reserve remaining marinade.
Grill skewers, often turning to make sure everything is cooked evenly. These can also be done in the broiler.

While grilling kabobs, combine vegetable stock, 1 tablespoon grated ginger, cumin, and salt. Bring to a light boil. Stir in couscous, raisins, and garbanzo beans; cover and remove from heat. Let sit for five minutes, or until fluffy. Just before serving, squeeze lemon over couscous and stir. Serve kabobs with reserved marinade.

name: Tempeh Stuffed Cremini Mushrooms
intro: Here’s a twist on stuffed mushrooms. There’s no bread or panko in the filling, just lots of flavor along with rice and tempeh.

ingredients.item: tempeh, diced very small, or pulsed small
15-ounce can chickpeas, drained (save the liquid to use as aquafaba) and rinsed

method: Remove stems from the mushrooms and set the caps aside. Finely chop the stems and set aside.

Heat 3 tablespoons of water in a medium skillet. Add the chopped mushroom stems and onion. Sauté 10 to 15 minutes or until onion is translucent. Add the tempeh and cook another 5 minutes. Add onion powder, cayenne pepper, rice, and tamari. Cook 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Stuff mushroom caps and place on baking sheet. Bake for 20 minutes.

name: Tempeh Tacos with Breaded and Baked Cauliflower
intro: Now’s the time for all good cooks to bake breaded cauliflower. There are so many layers of flavor that you could easily want to have two.

ingredients.item: plus 2 tablespoons unsweetened dairy-free milk, divided
15-ounce cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle pepper in adobo sauce (about 2 peppers), chopped
white corn taco shells or tortillas, or your favorite
Favorite toppings: spinach, lettuce, black olives, lime, avocado, peppers
diced red bell pepper (about one small pepper)
broccoli, inner stalks cut into cubes and florets cut into bites
canned black beans, drained and rinsed
sweet potato, peeled and chopped into bite-size pieces
dry white wine, such as chardonnay
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
small head cauliflower, cut into florets
small head broccoli, cut into florets
cooked black beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, chopped small, and 1 tablespoon adobo sauce
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
Steamed Seitan Chipotle Links, torn into bite-size pieces (page 284)
15-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into ½-inch cubes
Slow Cooker Versatile Seitan Balls, chopped (page 279)
Slow Cooker Versatile Seitan Balls, cubed (page 279)
15-ounce cans black beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, finely chopped
Additional toppings, such as more salsa, avocado or guacamole, and black olives
whole wheat or sprouted grain tortillas
Steamed Seitan Smoky Nuggets (page 283), cut into bite-size pieces if necessary
broccoli, stems peeled and diced, florets cut into bite-size pieces
cobs of corn, kernels cut from the cob
hot sauce, such as Tabasco (omit if you don’t like spicy; you can put it on the table instead)
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cubed
15-ounce cans black beans, drained and rinsed

method: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Cut the tempeh widthwise into ¼-inch strips, then tear those into about ½-inch pieces.
Mix 1 tablespoon hot sauce and 2 tablespoons milk together in a small bowl. Add tempeh and toss. Let marinate for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, prepare the cauliflower by cutting the florets into small bite-size pieces.
Mix 2 tablespoons of hot sauce and ¼ cup milk in a large bowl. Add the cauliflower and toss.
Add the flour, taco seasoning, panko, and nutritional yeast to a large bowl and mix well.

Take the cauliflower out of the wet mixture and add to the flour mixture and toss to coat all of the florets. Place on a baking sheet and bake for 20 to 30 minutes, turning after 15 minutes. You will be able to pierce them easily with a fork when done.

While the cauliflower is baking, heat the oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat and add the tempeh. Cook for about 2 minutes, flipping occasionally, until the pieces become golden brown. Remove from the heat to a paper towel.
Assemble the taco by laying some lettuce in the bottom of a shell and spooning in some tempeh, cauliflower, and tomato. Serve with lime wedges and salsa, if desired.

name: Tender Olive Oil Pastry Dough
servings: makes one (9 to 9½-inch / 23 to 24-cm) pie crust, tart crust, or freeform tart
intro: This update to my classic flaky pastry dough resulted from experiments with my favorite mild-tasting olive oil. I was delighted to discover that icy cold olive oil, just enough ice water, and two rest periods in the refrigerator to relax the gluten—this is where the magic happens!—created perfect pastry dough for sweet or savory pies and tarts. This crust is not difficult to make, but proper handling and careful attention to the directions are essential to its success.

ingredients.item: plus 1 tablespoon / 108 grams organic all-purpose flour
/ 103 grams organic whole wheat pastry flour
plus 1 tablespoon / 75 ml mild tasting extra-virgin olive oil, ice-cold, plus more at room temperature to grease the pie pan
to 2½ tablespoons / 30 to 38 ml ice water

method: Place a wire mesh strainer over a medium bowl. Whisk the flours in their containers to aerate, and measure the all-purpose flour and pastry flour into the strainer using the “whisk, dip, and sweep” method (page 63). Add the salt to the strainer and stir with a wire whisk to sift the ingredients into the bowl. (If any small bits remain in the strainer, add them to the mixture in the bowl.) Whisk to aerate the mixture.

Drizzle the cold oil over the flour mixture. Using a silicone spatula, toss until the oil is coated with flour. Do not break up the irregular fat pieces that form. These lumps are equivalent to the solid shortening used in conventional recipes and help to create a flaky crust.

In a small dish, stir the vinegar into 2 tablespoons of the ice water. Drizzle the liquid over the mass of dough and shake the bowl; this will get the water into the dough without extra handling—handling as little as possible is one of the important rules of making pie dough. Toss gently, using the spatula, until all the flour is moistened and a rough mass of dough holds together. Do not over mix. It is unlikely that more water will be needed, but if it is, use only as much as needed so that the dough holds together. Do not squeeze or press the dough into a round at this point.

It’s easier to roll half the dough at a time (and easier to find refrigerator space for 2 smaller pieces.) Turn half the dough at a time onto a large piece of plastic wrap. Enclose the dough lightly, allowing enough space for it to move freely. Pass a rolling pin over the dough until it is about 1 inch / 2.5 cm thick. Repeat with the other half. If you have extra-wide plastic wrap, you may wrap the dough in one piece. Rest the wrapped dough in the refrigerator for 45 minutes or up to 4 hours.

Shape the crust: Unwrap the dough but do not discard the plastic wrap. Cut off small pieces of dough with a sharp knife. (The pieces do not have to be uniform in size.) Scatter the pieces over the bottom of the pan and on the sides.

Cover the pan with a piece of plastic wrap. Flatten the pieces of dough with your fingertips by spreading them out until they form an even layer that covers the bottom and sides of the pan. Patch with extra dough as needed. Even out the dough by pressing on it with a flat-bottomed ½-measuring cup.

If using a pie pan, flute the edges. If using a tart pan, press the dough straight up the sides. Press lightly on the top edges of the pan with the cup to smooth the top ridge. Clean the outside of the pan of any dough. Wrap the dough in the pan lightly in plastic and refrigerate for 40 minutes or up to 4 hours before baking. Set a timer, and don’t let it go longer than 4 hours.
Blind bake the crust: Preheat your oven to 425°F / 220°C while the pie dough rests in the refrigerator. Position one rack in the lower third of the oven and another in the center.

Put the pie or tart pan on a baking sheet and remove the plastic wrap. Do not prick the dough. Cut a square of parchment paper slightly larger than the pie pan. Crumple the paper to make it more flexible, and place it on the pie dough. Put a piece of heavy duty foil on top of the parchment paper, shiny side down, and fill with pie weights or dried beans used for this purpose.

name: Tex-Mex Beef Tacos
method: Heat a large frying pan, and then cook the mince.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add oil to the pan and fry the garlic, oregano and spices for a few
minutes.
Heat the taco shells.
Add cilantro, avocado slices and red onion on top.
Your dish is ready to be served.

name: Tex-Mex Breakfast Taco

source.author: Various
source.chapter: Welcome to the World of Mexican Taco Breakfast Recipes

ingredients.item: Freshly chopped parsley and cilantro, two tbsp.

method: Add a little olive oil in the pan.
Cut the tomatoes, jalapenos, onions, and cilantro.
Cook the Smithfield Breakfast Sausage per package instructions.
Add the beaten eggs and scramble, set aside.
Chop the potatoes into small cubes and cook with a little bit of olive
oil, garlic, salt and pepper until they are slightly crispy.
Heat the tortilla in a frying pan and add the shredded cheese.
Combine the potatoes, eggs, and sausage and mix well.
Serve your dish with fresh salsa.

category.chapter: Welcome to the World of Mexican Taco Breakfast Recipes

name: Tex- Mex Vegetarian Tacos

ingredients.item: Freshly chopped parsley and cilantro, two tbsp.

method: Add a little olive oil in the pan.
Cut the tomatoes, jalapenos, onions, and cilantro.
Cook the red bell pepper, green bell pepper, peas, and red onion.
Chop the potatoes into small cubes and cook with a little bit of olive
oil, garlic, salt and pepper until they are slightly crispy.
Heat the tortilla in a frying pan and add the shredded cheese.
Combine the potatoes, and mix vegetables.
Add the ingredients on the tortillas.
Top with sour cream, and cilantro creamy sauce.
Serve your dish with fresh salsa.

name: Texas Caviar on Grilled Rustic Bread
intro: ONE OF THE MANY creative ways that Southerners use black-eyed peas is to combine them with tomato, bell pepper, and onion and tossing with a tangy vinaigrette to create Texas caviar. Although often eaten as a dip with chips, as one would enjoy tomato salsa, I spoon mine on thick slices of rustic bread that have been grilled or toasted and garnish each slice with crispy garlic and garlic oil, which makes for a party-perfect appetizer. This recipe yields a large quantity with summer gatherings in mind. Red Summer cocktails would be the perfect accompaniment.

ingredients.item: whole sun-dried tomatoes, or scant ¼ cup diced sun-dried tomatoes
dried black-eyed peas, sorted and soaked in water overnight
diced seeded heirloom tomatoes, in ¼-inch pieces
diced green bell pepper, in ¼-inch pieces
diced yellow bell pepper, in ¼-inch pieces
diced red onion, in ¼-inch pieces
jalapeño chiles, seeded and diced into ¼-inch pieces
large loaf rustic bread, cut into about twelve ½- to ¾-inch-thick slices

method: Put the sun-dried tomatoes in a small heatproof bowl and add boiling water to cover. Cover and let soak for 5 minutes.

Drain the black-eyed peas and rinse them well. Transfer to a medium saucepan and add water to cover by 2 inches. Bring to a boil over high heat. Decrease the heat to medium, skim off any foam, and partially cover. Cook until the beans are softening but still firm, 40 to 50 minutes. Stir in 1 teaspoon of the salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Drain in a colander, rinse under cold water for 1 minute, and let cool.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a medium skillet over low heat. Add the garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy and golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Strain the garlic oil through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl and reserve the garlic and the oil separately.

Drain the sun-dried tomatoes, chop finely, and put in a blender. Add the lemon juice, vinegar, and the remaining ¾ teaspoon salt and process until smooth. With the blender running, pour in ¼ cup of the garlic oil in a slow stream and process until creamy.

Transfer the blended mixture to a large bowl. Add the black-eyed peas, tomatoes, green and yellow bell peppers, onion, jalapeños, and half of the cilantro. Stir gently until well combined, then cover and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Season the black-eyed pea mixture with black pepper and, if desired, more salt.

Lightly brush each slice of bread with garlic oil, saving any leftover for drizzling. Put the bread on a large baking sheet and bake, without turning, until lightly browned and toasted on top, 6 to 10 minutes. Top each slice with 2 heaping tablespoons of the black-eyed pea mixture. Garnish with a few slices of crispy garlic and a scattering of the remaining cilantro. Drizzle with garlic oil and enjoy.

name: Thai Beef Stir-Fry
intro: A unique peanut sauce complements the colorful combination of tender sirloin, cauliflower, carrots, broccoli and mushrooms. I like to serve it over spaghetti, but fried noodles work well too.
method: In a small bowl, combine the brown sugar, cornstarch, beef broth, soy sauce, onion powder, garlic powder, ground ginger, and hot pepper sauce until smooth.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a large cast iron skillet or wok, then sauté the beef until the meat is no longer pink. Transfer the beef to a plate.
In the same wok, heat the remaining oil, then sauté the broccoli, cauliflowers, and carrots for 5 minutes.
Sauté the mushrooms for 3-5 minutes.
Add the soup mixture (Step 1) to the wok. Let it boil. Cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium, then add ground beef (Step 2) and peanut butter. Cook, stirring, until the peanut butter is incorporated.
Serve with pasta and top with peanuts before eating.

name: Thai Chicken and Slaw
intro: This recipe is very easy and worth the time it takes to prepare. Kids will love the sweetness of the honey. You can also omit the chicken from the recipe so that your vegetarian friends can enjoy it too.
method: In a small bowl, whisk the canola oil, white wine vinegar, honey, gingerroot, soy sauce, garlic cloves, and sesame oil until combined.
Pour 1 cup of the mixture into a bowl or shallow dish. Add the chicken into the mixture and marinate (refrigerated) overnight. Cover the rest of the mixture and refrigerate.
Drain the chicken and discard the mixture from the bowl.
Coat a 13x9-inch pan with cooking spray. Place the chicken in the pan and bake, uncovered, at 350°F for 30-40 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine the coleslaw, edamame, and chopped bell pepper in a large bowl.
Add peanut butter and salt to the remaining mixture and stir until combined. Pour over coleslaw mixture and toss well. Refrigerate until serving.
Serve the chicken with the salad. Top with green onions.

name: Thai Chicken Lettuce Wraps
intro: This recipe is tasty and delicious. It's also fun to put the salad together.
method: Add the rice vinegar, mayonnaise, creamy peanut butter, brown sugar, soy sauce, gingerroot, chili sauce, and garlic clove in a blender and blend.
Gradually add the oil in a steady steam into the blender as it processes. When done, stir in the cilantro.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, red pepper, onions, carrot and 1/4 cup peanuts.
Add dressing (Step 2) and toss well.
Distribute the mixture (Step 4) equally between the lettuce leaves.
Top each leaf with the remaining peanuts. Before serving, fold the lettuce to wrap the fillings.

name: Thai Chicken Peanut Noodles
intro: I love the spiciness of these Thai chicken noodles and often use chopsticks for a more immersive experience.
method: Whisk peanut butter, chicken broth, lemon juice, soy sauce, chili sauce, and red pepper flakes in a small bowl until smooth.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Strain when done
In a large skillet, fry the carrots, pepper, garlic, and chicken over medium heat for 5-6 mins.
Stir in peanut butter mixture (Step 1). Let it boil. When it starts boiling, reduce heat and let it simmer for 3-5 mins.
Serve the mixture (Step 4) with pasta. Top with green onions and peanuts.

name: Thai Coconut Beef
intro: Love Thai food but have no time to eat outside on a weeknight due to your busy schedules? You can make a double serving of this dish – one for tonight’s dinner, and another for tomorrow’s lunch. In my opinion, it is best to use beef, but it would be just as delicious if you used chicken or pork!
method: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Place the beef pieces and peppers into a slow cooker.
Mix all the beef seasoning ingredients in a bowl, then pour over the meat.
Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours.
Remove beef from the slow cooker and let it cool down a bit. Remove the fat from the reserved juice. Shred the beef with 2 forks.
Add the beef and beans to the slow cooker. Cover and cook for another 45-60 minutes.
Add coriander and stir. Serve with rice

name: Thai Iced Tea
intro: is probably the most famous brand of tea mix in Thailand but if you can’t source it, substitutions

ingredients.item: Ginger, large hand sized root (8 oz/200 g) peeled, the older the better

method: Cut up the ginger and place in a big pot of water on the stove. Sim- mer over low heat for at least 2 hours, until the water is infused with the ginger.
Drain and drink hot imme- diately, or save in the freezer for whenever you need it. If you prefer it a little sweet, just add a teaspoon of sugar or honey.
This ginger drink, when sweet- ened, is also a good base for fresh tofu and deep-fried dough bits—a common street food breakfast.
½ cup (125 ml) lime juice (fresh preferable)
1 cup (250 ml) soda water
1 cup (250 ml) water
1 cup (200 g) sugar

name: Thai Marinated Grilled Steak
intro: Although this is a classic Thai steak marinade, the flavor is neutral enough to serve with any dish. Rich in flavor and infinitely customizable, this is the only marinade recipe you'll ever need. The dipping sauce is an irresistible classic for Thais!

ingredients.item: the Nam Jim Jeaw Dipping Sauce:

method: Grind the black peppercorns and garlic in a mortar.
To make the marinade, combine the black peppercorns, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, lime juice, and oil in a large bowl.

Place the steaks into the marinade. Move the steak around to make sure it's coated properly. Let it marinate (refrigerated) for at least 3 hours (better if overnight). When done, remove steak from the refrigerator and let it rest for 1 hour.
Grill the steak to your liking.
To make the dipping sauce, combine the fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and tamarind in a small bowl. Stir well.
Add onions and chili flakes into the bowl. Don't worry if lumps of sugar don’t dissolve.
To make toasted rice powder, stir-fry the rice in a dry skillet over medium heat until grains are dark brown.
When done, pour the rice onto a plate to cool, then grind it to a fine powder with a mortar and pestle or coffee grinder.
Add the rice powder (Step 8) and coriander into the sauce (Step 6). You may serve the steak with the Nam Jim Jeaw dipping sauce or keep the Nam Jim Jeaw dipping sauce for future use.

name: Thai Pasta with Spicy Peanut Sauce
intro: Embrace the wholesome goodness of whole grain pasta paired with crisp green vegetables, all coated in a luscious and creamy peanut sauce. The addition of fresh lime juice adds a zesty and invigorating touch to this dish. While some prefer to enjoy it hot, you can also savor its flavors when it has cooled to room temperature. Either way, this dish promises a delightful and satisfying culinary experience.
method: Cook linguine according to package directions. Strain it once done.
In a small bowl, combine the peanut butter and lemon juice.
Add peanut butter mixture (Step 1), all the vegetables, linguine (Step 1), and cilantro to skillet. Toss well.

name: Thai Red Curry Chicken and Vegetables
intro: The key to this chicken curry is to get the complex flavors. For vegetables, I like to use peanuts, sweet red peppers, and water chestnuts

ingredients.item: Cubed boneless skinless chicken breast - 1 ½ pounds

method: Place chicken in an oiled 8-inch square baking dish.
In a small bowl, combine coconut milk, curry, and salt. Pour over chicken.

Place the chicken in an oven-safe dish and cover it. Bake the chicken in a preheated oven at 425°F (220°C) for 18-22 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and reaches the desired internal temperature. While the chicken is baking, prepare the vegetables according to the package directions, ensuring they are cooked to perfection.
Serve the chicken (Step 3) with rice and vegetables (Step 4).

name: Thai Red Lentil Soup with Aromatic Chile Oil

ingredients.item: medium onion, thinly sliced (1½ cups/160 g)
lemongrass stalks, gently bashed with a rolling pin
cup/15 g cilantro leaves, coarsely chopped salt
banana shallot, or 2 regular shallots, coarsely chopped (½ cup/50 g)
peeled and coarsely chopped fresh ginger
tomato paste grated zest of ½ small lemon

method: First make the chile oil. Heat 2 tablespoons of the sunflower oil in a small saucepan. Add the shallot, garlic, ginger, chile, star anise, and curry powder and fry over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring from time to time, until the shallot is soft. Add the tomato paste and cook gently for 2 minutes. Stir in the remaining oil and the lemon zest and simmer very gently for 30 minutes.
Leave to cool and then strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve.

For the soup, bring a small pan of water to a boil and throw in the sugar snap peas. Cook for 90 seconds, drain, refresh under cold water, and set aside to dry. Once cool, cut them on the diagonal into slices
/16-inch/2-mm thick.

Heat the sunflower oil in a large pot and add the onion. Cook over low heat, with a lid on, for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the onion is completely soft and sweet. Stir in the red curry paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, red lentils, and 3 cups/700 ml water. Bring to a boil, turn down the heat to low, and simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft.
Remove the soup from the heat and take out and discard the lemongrass and lime leaves. Use a blender to process the soup until it is completely smooth.
Add the coconut milk, lime juice, soy sauce, and ½ teaspoon salt and stir.

Return the soup to medium heat, and once the soup is almost boiling, ladle into bowls. Scatter the snap peas on top, sprinkle with the cilantro, and finish with ½ teaspoon chile oil drizzled over each portion.

name: Thai Salad with Peanut Sauce
intro: A fresh and delicious Thai salad accompanied with a satisfying crunch from the peanut sauce
method: In a large bowl, toss all the salad ingredients.
To make the dressing, whisk all the peanut dressing ingredients (except the dry roasted peanut and jalapeno pepper) in a small bowl.
Add the dressing to salad mixture (Step 1) and mix well.
Divide salad between 4 plates. Top with peanuts and jalapeños.

name: Thai Salmon Brown Rice
intro: This quick salmon recipe is a pretty straightforward recipe. A store-bought dressing gives this healthy dish an enhanced flavor, without significantly lengthening the preparation time.
method: Place salmon on a 15×10×1-inch pan.
Brush with 1/4 cup dressing. Bake for 8-10 minutes at 400°F
Stir the rice with coriander and salt.
Divide rice mixture (Step 3) between 4 bowls. Add salmon, carrots, cabbage, and the remaining dressing onto each rice bowls.

name: Thai Shrimp Salad
intro: Here’s a deliciously different salad that combines grilled shrimp (a lean protein source) with low-calorie cucumbers and onions. It is made with a refreshing Thai blend of sesame seeds, coriander, lime and mint.

ingredients.item: A dash of crushed red pepper flakes
Peeled and deveined uncooked large shrimp

method: In a large bowl, combine the lime juice, sesame oil, soy sauce, sesame seeds, mint, cilantro, and red pepper flakes.
Sprinkle shrimp with salt and pepper. Thread the shrimps onto 2 metal or soaked wooden skewers.
Place skewers on an oiled grill. Cover and cook over medium heat for 2 to 4 minutes.
Add shrimp, onion, and cucumber into the sauce (Step 1) and stir well.
Divide lettuce leaf between 2 salad plates and top each one of them with shrimp mixture (Step 4). Serve immediately.

name: Thai Shrimp Soup
intro: This delicious soup is ready in minutes and is a hit. Its ingredients are also available at most grocery store, big or small
method: Heat oil in a Dutch oven, then sauté the onion until soft.
Add water, lemongrass, curry leaves, ginger, fish sauce, brown sugar, and chicken broth. Let it boil. When it starts boiling, reduce heat and add the edamame and shrimp. Cook for 5-6 mins, uncovered.
Add coconut milk, sorghum, bamboo shoots, basil, cilantro, lime juice, and lime peel. Let it boil. Discard the lemongrass before serving.

name: Thai Shrimp Stir-Fry
intro: Elevate your culinary experience with this vibrant dish that combines the flavors of Thai cuisine. The delightful combination of red pepper, snow peas, and shrimp is enhanced by the rich and flavorful peanut sauce. A touch of ginger and red pepper flakes adds an extra kick of deliciousness. To complete the dish, serve this colorful main course over a bed of pasta, creating a fusion of Thai and Italian influences that will surely impress your taste buds.
method: Heat canola oil in a large non-stick skillet or wok, then sauté the red pepper for 1 minute.
Sauté the snow peas, scallions, and garlic for 2-3 minutes. When done, transfer the mixture to a plate.
In the same wok, combine broth, paprika, ginger, sesame oil, vinegar, soy sauce, and peanut butter. Cook and stir until the peanut butter melts and the mixture starts boiling.
Add shrimp and cook (stirring) for 2 minutes.
Return red pepper mixture (Step 2) to the wok.
Serve with fettuccine.

name: Thai-spiced lamb salad with lime dressing
intro: The vibrant colors of this spicy lamb salad really sing out, making it perfect for a summer lunch. Be sure not to overcook the lamb, or slice into it without letting it rest first, or you’ll risk losing those delicious meat juices.

ingredients.item: (For the dressing) grated zest and juice of 5 limes
(For the dressing) palm sugar or brown sugar
(For the dressing) red chile, seeded and finely chopped

method: For the dressing, place the lime zest and juice, sugar, chile, fish sauce, tamarind, and 1 tablespoon of peanut oil in a small bowl. Mix to combine all the ingredients and dissolve the sugar. Set aside.

Cut the lamb into eight equal strips. Heat a grill pan and add the remaining groundnut oil. Sear the lamb for about 2 minutes on each side. Do not overcook the lamb—it should be rare. Let rest for 3 minutes.

Slice the lamb thinly and place in a large bowl. Add the glass noodles, dressing, shallots, herbs, and peanuts, and toss to combine. Divide the salad between 4 individual plates and serve immediately.

name: Thai Spinach Beef Salad
intro: This is a fun salad to eat. It is crunchy, dense, and a little spicy. Most importantly, it's good for you.
method: To make the sauce, combine the lime juice, brown sugar, soy sauce, basil, mint, and gingerroot until combined.
Heat a large non-stick skillet coated with cooking spray over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the beef and jalapeños for 1-3 minutes.
Stir-fry the garlic for 1 minute. Turn off the heat when done.
Add spinach, red pepper, cucumber, beef mixture (Step 3) to a large bowl. Drizzle the sauce (Step 1) over it and mix well. Serve immediately.

name: Thai sticky rice with crispy ginger, chile, and peanuts
intro: Sticky rice is brilliant as it is, served alongside all sorts of sh and meat dishes, but

ingredients.item: 2-inch/5cm piece of ginger, peeled and julienned (5 tbsp/40g)
cups/30g cilantro stems, cut into 1¼-inch/3cm lengths
salted and roasted peanuts, roughly chopped
lime, cut into 6 wedges, to serve

method: Put the rice into a medium saucepan with a well-tting lid, along with ½ tsp salt and the water. Bring to a boil, then decrease the heat to medium-low and simmer gently, covered, for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside, still covered, for 5 minutes.

While the rice is cooking, put the oil into a medium frying pan and place over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the ginger, garlic and chiles and fry for 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently, until just starting to brown. Add the cilantro, peanuts, sesame seeds, and a generous pinch of salt and continue to fry for
1–2 minutes, until golden brown. Spoon over the rice and serve, with the wedges of lime alongside.
Baked rice with confit tomatoes and garlic
This was my go-to side for a good few months, working well with pretty much anything else on the table. There’s also enough going on, avorwise, for it to be lovely as it is, as a main.

Peeling so many garlic cloves won’t win me any “simple” brownie points, I know, but, once done, the simple joy of this dish is that the rice is baked in the oven rather than on the stove. For those who nd creating perfectly cooked rice in a pan of simmering water strangely difficult, this will be a revelation. Just make sure the foil is sealed tightly over the dish—you don’t want any steam to escape in the oven.

name: Thai-Style Brisket
intro: This is an incredible brisket that will blow your mind. Peanut butter, soy, crunchy vegetables and spicy sauce give it the authentic Thai taste we love.
method: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, then fry the brisket on both sides.
Transfer the meat and its drippings to a 5-quart slow cooker.
In a small bowl, combine peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, cilantro, lemon juice, garlic, pepper flakes and paprika
Pour the sauce (Step 3) over brisket. Cover the slow cooker and cook for 8 to 9 hours on low heat. When done, remove the brisket from the slow cooker.
Combine cornstarch and water in a bowl until smooth
Add the cornstarch (Step 5) into the slow cooker. Cover the slow cooker and cook on high for 30 minutes.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet or sauté pan, then sauté the carrots, peppers, and onions until crisp-tender. You may want to add peanuts too.
Add the cooking juices (Step 6) into the vegetable mixture (Step 7) and mix well.
Cut the meat into thin slices.

name: Thai-style Chicken Biryani
intro: family gatherings. It’s quite labor-intensive, but has been simplifi ed considerably (!) from the

ingredients.item: times until the water becomes clear. Add the rice to the pot once the water is boiling, and cook for 5 minutes. Pour the rice into a colan- der to drain the water. Add a pinch of saff ron to the rice and mix in.

method: Add all but 2 tablespoons of the ghee evenly over the rice, and save the charcoal and reserved ghee for later use.

Place a small 1½ inch (4 cm) heat proof bowl or ramekin on top of the rice. Add the ghee-soaked charcoal to the bowl and light it on fi re. The ghee should readily burn, allowing the charcoal to become red-hot again. Once the ember is glowing, pour the reserved ghee onto the charcoal to create smoke.
Quickly place a lid or aluminum foil onto the Dutch oven/baking dish to trap the smoke.
Place into a oven preheated to
325° F (160° C) for 35–40 minutes.

Check that the chicken is fully cooked. Remove the bowl with charcoal. With a fork fl uff the top of the rice. Assemble the rice and chicken onto a serving platter with the remaining thinly sliced mint leaves and crispy shallots, if using.
Serve with the Pickled Cucumbers.
This is actually one of three (!) garam masala recipes in the family cookbook. Since the other two recipes yield such huge quantities of spice, I opted for this one.
4 tablespoons cumin powder
3 tablespoons cinnamon powder
1 tablespoon clove powder
1 tablespoon cardamom powder
Combine all and mix well.
10 mini cucumbers, cut in half vertically and each piece cut in half horizontally to form spears
2 tablespoons ginger, fi nely julienned
2 tablespoons red shallots, thinly sliced
1 each green, orange and red fi nger- length chilies, seeds scraped out and thinly sliced
½ cup (125 ml) white vinegar
½ cup (100 g) sugar
Arrange the cucumber spears in a pan big enough to hold them all and scatter the ginger, shallots and chilies over the top.
Mix the vinegar, salt, and sugar together in a small saucepan. Heat over medium heat until it comes to a low boil. Wait for the sugar and salt to dissolve before turning off the heat. Allow to cool.
Pour the vinegar mixture over the cucumbers and cover. Keep in a cool and dry place. Leave to pick- le for at least 2 hours. Serve on the side with the Chicken Biryani.
SOUTHERN-STYLE FAVORITES

name: Thai-Style Green Beans
intro: Peanut butter, soy sauce and hoisin sauce give this delicious bean dish a nice boost in flavor.
method: Mix all the sauce ingredients in a bowl.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, then sauté the onion and ginger for 2 minutes.
Sauté the green beans for 3 minutes.
Add the green bean (Step 3) to the sauce. Stir well. You may want to top it with cilantro and peanuts.

name: Thai-Style Sweet-and-Sour Soup

ingredients.item: or 5 makrut lime leaves, roughly torn into chunks, center stems removed
straw or white button mushrooms, rinsed in salted water and halved
enoki mushrooms, stems trimmed and rinsed in salted water

method: Soak tamarind pulps in the hot water for about 15 minutes. Use a spoon to break up the pulps, press through a strainer to get a tamarind paste, and then discard the fibrous part. Set aside.

Trim off the green upper parts and lowest, toughest portions at the bases of the lemongrass stalks. Place on a cutting board and bruise the bulbous end with a pestle or meat tenderizer to release fragrance and flavor.
Cut tofu into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes and set aside.

Heat oil in a 2-quart (2 L) saucepan over medium-low heat. When hot, add the leeks and cook and stir until fragrant (about 30 seconds). Add lemongrass stalks, tomatoes, 4 cups (1 L) of water, salt, stock powder, sugar, and lime leaves to the pan and bring to a boil.

Stir in tamarind paste and tofu, and season with vegan fish sauce (if using) or more salt. Continue to boil until the tomatoes are tender (3 to 5 minutes). During the last minute of cooking, separate the mushrooms into bite-size bunches and stir them in. When soup returns to a boil, remove from heat.
Transfer soup to bowls and serve hot.

name: Thai Sweet Chili Tofu Stacks
intro: In preparation for a party, make your life easier by using some prepackaged ingredients. You and your guests will love these beautiful skewers of marinated tofu, with lots of flavor in each bite.

ingredients.item: chili pepper, such as jalapeño or cayenne, chopped fine
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into 1-inch cubes
seitan, crumbled (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
28-ounce can chickpeas, drained (save the liquid to use as aquafaba) and rinsed
raw almonds, soaked in water from one hour to overnight
extra virgin olive oil, more if desired
seitan, crumbled (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
medium sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped into 2-inch cubes (equal to 2 cups mashed sweet potato)
14-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
tapioca starch or tapioca flour (they are the same thing)
15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
hot chili pepper, sliced thin crosswise
baby spinach, with stems chopped off
seitan (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
tempeh, diced very small, or pulsed small
15-ounce can chickpeas, drained (save the liquid to use as aquafaba) and rinsed

method: Prepare the sauce by mixing the cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of water together until smooth and set aside.
Add the rice vinegar, ⅔ cup water, sugar, chili pepper, garlic, tamari, parsley, and cayenne pepper to a food processor. Process until well blended and the chili pepper is broken up very well.

Pour mixture into a small saucepan and heat until boiling, stirring until the sugar is dissolved. Turn down heat and cook 5 minutes. Add the cornstarch mixture and stir occasionally for about 5 minutes or until mixture is a bit thickened. Take off heat and let it cool.
Add the tofu cubes to the cooled sweet chili sauce. Let marinate about 30 minutes.
Drain the pineapple and slice the rings into about 1- to 1¼-inch wedges.
Place a slice of pineapple on a plate and center a cube of marinated tofu on top. Place another slice of pineapple on the tofu and secure with a toothpick.

name: Thai Sweet Rolls
intro: Chris Schultz came up with this sweet roll recipe to pair with the coconut ice cream.

ingredients.item: can sweetened condensed milk (add to taste)

method: Add the condensed milk to taste—the sweeter it is, the more
“authentic” it is. Add a pinch of ground cardamom to each cup before serving.
4 cups (1 l) water
6 heaping tablespoons Thai tea mix (like Cha Tra Mue). If you can’t fi nd Cha Tra Mue steep the following in 4 cups (1 l) water:
4 tablespoons loose-leaf black tea (or 4 tea bags), 2 star anise pod,
4 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, pinch of turmeric,
½ vanilla bean or 1 teaspoon extract (almond extract may be substituted), tamarind powder, to taste (if you can get it)

name: Thalipeeth
intro: Thalipeeth is one of the most underrated Indian breads, and making it is nothing short of an art. It’s not rolled out like regular rotis—instead, it is patted into shape on a plate, which is where it gets its name from: thali (plate), peeth (patting). I like an extra crusty and textured version of the thalipeeth instead of soft breads.
method: In a bowl, mix all the ingredients, except the oil. Add water and knead the mixture into a medium-soft dough.
Pull out a portion of the dough and flatten it with the palms of your hands.
Continue flattening it on an even surface until round and flat, yet thick.
Make impressions in the flattened dough with your index finger and cook the dough on a hot pan with a tsp of oil for 3-4 minutes on medium flame.

name: The Heart of Dishes Sofrito!
intro: Deseed your bell peppers and roughly chop them along with the tomato and onion. Remove the stems from the oregano, cilantro and culantro, and roughly chop them as well.

ingredients.item: Leaves from a few sprigs oregano
Salt and freshly ground black pepper (optional)

method: Sofrito is so important to many dishes that I make. It is the foundation that ties everything together and gives the dish its flair and sabor. Sofrito is an aromatic blend of vegetables, herbs and spices used to flavor beans, fish, meats, rice and stews. It is used in many Hispanic cultures and each person makes it differently and calls it by different names. Sofrito can be found in most markets in the freezer aisle, but there is nothing like making it fresh and storing it at home or even sharing it with your friends and family. A few tips here: If you cannot find ají dulce peppers, substitute 2 Cubanelle peppers. Feel free to scale the number of garlic cloves up or down. I always say to use a shit ton, but you should make it your own. If you cannot find culantro, double up on the cilantro instead.

Use a good blender to blend your vegetables, one vegetable at a time (you do not want the blender to overflow), as follows: Blend your green and red bell peppers first, then place in a bowl. Then blend your tomato, ají dulces, garlic and oregano. Add the onion, cilantro, culantro and mini sweet peppers, blend again, then place in the same bowl. You can add oil to aid in the blending, but don’t use too much, about 2 tablespoons (30 ml) should suffice. The juice from the vegetables should be enough to blend everything together. If you want, add salt and black pepper to taste.

Once everything is combined and mixed well, you can freeze it in freezer-safe jars until you need to use it. Sofrito will stay good in the freezer for about 6 months, or in the refrigerator for about 2 weeks. ¡Buen provecho!

name: The No-Oil-Added Chocolate Torte to Live For
intro: Full disclosure: as a rule, I do not make or enjoy eating so-called fat-free cakes. I find the texture gummy when one hundred percent of the fat is replaced by fruit purée. And the fact that more sugar is necessary in oil-free, fruit purée-added baked goods is off-putting as well. So, when my daughter Tracy called to tell me she’d forgotten the oil in my Chocolate Torte to Live For recipe and liked the cake, I doubted her assessment, although she is one smart cookie and a baker. “No,” she insisted, “It’s denser and different, Mom, but really good.” Still, I didn’t intend to try “Tracy’s recipe” until I was invited to present dessert demonstrations at the McDougall Celebrity Chef Weekend in Santa Rosa, California, where oils are prohibited in recipes. The cake was a resounding success and I have served it many times since. Sometime later, though, I decided to try using some canned coconut milk in the recipe. I’m not suggesting this change fits into a very lowfat eating plan, but I do prefer the taste and texture of this variation. The final word I leave to you. In keeping with the no-oil-added theme of this cake, I suggest frosting with Bittersweet Chocolate Ganache Glaze (page 264), which is naturally oil-free and low in sugar.

ingredients.item: minus 1 tablespoon / 60 grams organic whole wheat pastry flour
/ 9 grams arrowroot or organic cornstarch (10.5 grams)
plus 1 tablespoon / 31 grams Dutch-process cocoa powder
/ 50 grams organic granulated sugar, finely ground in a blender
unsweetened canned full-fat coconut milk, well-stirred (do not use light)
pure maple syrup, Grade B or dark amber

method: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°F / 180°C. Oil the sides and bottom of the cake pan, and line the bottom with a parchment circle. Do not oil the parchment.

Place a wire mesh strainer over a medium bowl. Add the all-purpose flour, pastry flour, arrowroot, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon to the strainer. Stir with a wire whisk to sift the ingredients into the bowl. (If any small bits remain in the strainer, add them to the mixture in the bowl). Whisk to aerate.

In a separate medium bowl, whisk the coconut milk, almond milk, maple syrup, vanilla, chocolate extract (if using), and vinegar until completely blended. Pour into the dry mixture and whisk until the batter is smooth. Pour the batter into the pan.

Bake on the center rack for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the top is set, the sides have started to pull away from the pan, and a wooden toothpick or skewer inserted into the center comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs.

Cool the pan on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Run a thin knife between the cake and inside of the pan, and invert onto a rack. Remove the pan and carefully peel off the parchment paper. Invert again, top side up on the rack to cool completely. Refrigerate the cake briefly before glazing.

name: The Perfect Matcha Latte
intro: You can make the perfect matcha latte at home with a blender; you’ll get a delicious, fluffy foam. Try it—I know you’ll like it! For best results, use the white almond butter, or replace it with unsalted cashew butter. You can use almond mylk or other vegetable-based milk, but then you should omit the nut butter and the water.
method: Put the matcha powder, honey, and almond butter in the blender. Add water, and mix.

name: The Simplest Raw Brownie
intro: Once you’ve tried this recipe, you’ll wonder how something so simple can taste so good! This raw brownie easily beats regular brownies, both in wholesomeness and in flavor.
method: Pulverize 1 cup (2 dl) walnuts in the food processor. Remove the pits from the dates. Add in the dates, cacao powder and salt, and process until you have a dough. Stir in the remaining walnuts. Press the dough into a small mold, or shape it into a square and cut into smaller squares. Store in the refrigerator.

name: The Ultimate Breakfast Paratha
intro: As a paratha stan, I simply had no choice in creating this recipe. I simply don’t know what I did before my frozen paratha obsession began. Well, it’s more like a lifestyle at this point. They are the perfect freezable food, just as good as fresh when fried, and so versatile. I’ve used them for desserts, as pitta-style chips … the list goes on. Here, I’ve used them as a vessel for ackee and plantain. While writing this book, this was my weekend brekky after one too many frozen margs the night before. I’ve made them for friends that stayed the night and made paratha addicts out of them, too. This recipe includes a different twist on vegan ackee and ‘salt fish’, using artichokes. This dish is often served with fried dumplings or hard food, and the paratha offers a wonderful twist.

ingredients.item: olive oil, plus extra for frying the plantains
spring onion (scallion), chopped, plus extra to serve
ripe plantains, peeled and sliced diagionally into 8 pieces
splash of your favourite hot sauce, to taste

method: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan (skillet) over a medium heat and add the onion with a pinch of salt and sweat for 2–3 minutes until softened. Add the tomato, Scotch bonnet, spring onion, garlic and thyme and fry for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Now add the artichokes and fry for a further minute. Add a splash of water to the pan to deglaze and then reduce to a simmer. Add the ackee, cover and steam for 5 minutes.
In a separate frying pan, heat enough oil to coat over a medium heat and fry the plantain slices for 3–4 minutes until golden, flipping to cook each side.
Mix together all the ingredients for the yoghurt in a small bowl.
Heat a dry frying pan over a medium heat and cook the paratha, one at a time, for 1–2 minutes on each side.
Place a paratha on a plate, add a dollop of the spicy yoghurt, some plantain and then the ackee mixture. Garnish with some more spring onions or hot sauce.

name: The Ultimate Jamaican Breakfast
intro: Fried dumplings remind me of Sunday mornings. That was fried dumpling time for my mother, and waking up to that smell was heavenly. You wouldn’t make this full version on a weekly basis – often I would have the dumplings with steamed cabbage and salt fish, or even sausages and spicy baked beans. The recipe below is with all the bells and whistles. With ackee and salt fish being the national dish of Jamaica, it would feel strange to not include a recipe for it. It feels like a ‘I’m trying to impress my partner’s family’ kind of moment, or ‘it’s Easter and I’ve been put in charge of breakfast’.

ingredients.item: self-raising flour (or 4 cups all-purpose flour plus 3½ teaspoons baking powder)
tin of ackee, rinsed and drained
salt and freshly ground black pepper
your favourite hot sauce, to serve
ripe plantains, peeled and sliced diagonally into 8 pieces
olive or vegetable oil, for frying

method: First make the dumplings. Put the flour, sugar and salt (and baking powder if using all-purpose flour) into a bowl with the butter. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the dry ingredients. Add the water to bring it together, then knead in the bowl until you have a smooth dough. Cover with cling film (plastic wrap) and leave to rest for 1 hour. This will allow the gluten to fully hydrate and give you the fluﬃest dumplings. Once rested, separate the dough into eight pieces, then form into balls by rolling in your hands. Set back in the bowl.

Next prepare the ackee and ‘salt fish’. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan (skillet) over a medium heat. Sweat the onion for 2–3 minutes with a pinch of salt until softened, then add the tomato, Scotch bonnet, spring onion, garlic and thyme. Fry for a few more minutes until wonderfully fragrant. Now add the heart of palm and season with the vegan fish sauce. Fry for another minute. Add a splash of water to the pan to deglaze and then reduce the heat to a simmer. Add the ackee, cover with a lid and steam for 5 minutes.
For the plantains, in a separate frying pan, heat enough oil to coat over a medium heat and fry the plantain slices for 3–4 minutes until golden, flipping to cook each side.

Now make the garlicky greens. Heat the butter in a frying pan and once melted fry the garlic until fragrant. Add the kale and a splash of water. Season with salt and pepper, cover and steam for 2 minutes. Next add the spinach, put the lid back on and cook until just wilted. Check for seasoning.

Heat 2.5 cm (1 inch) of oil in a deep-sided heavy-bottomed frying pan over a medium heat. Test the temperature by using a wooden spoon – if lots of bubbles appear around it immediately, it’s ready to go. Fry the dumplings for 3–4 minutes – be careful, if they are browning too quickly, the temperature of the oil is too high.
Put a couple of fried dumplings, some plantains and garlicky greens on each plate. Finally, add the ackee and ‘salt fish’ in the middle. Serve with your favourite hot sauce and enjoy!

name: The ultimate winter couscous
intro: Someone complained to the Guardian about the long list of ingredients in this recipe. But I knew it was a success when a friend spotted it on the menu (with a due credit) of the Sun and Doves, a cool and arty pub in Camberwell.

ingredients.item: medium carrots, peeled and cut into ¾-inch chunks
medium parsnips, peeled and cut into ¾-inch chunks
cubed pumpkin or butternut squash (from a 10 oz squash)

method: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Place the carrots, parsnips and shallots in a large ovenproof dish. Add the cinnamon sticks, star anise, bay leaves, 4 tablespoons of the oil, ¾ teaspoon salt and all the other spices and mix well. Place in the oven and cook for 15 minutes.

Add the pumpkin, stir and return to the oven. Continue cooking for about 35 minutes, by which time the vegetables should have softened while retaining a bite. Now add the dried apricots and the chickpeas with their cooking liquid and/or water. Return to the oven and cook for a further 10 minutes, or until hot.

About 15 minutes before the vegetables are ready, put the couscous in a large heatproof bowl with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, the saffron and ½ teaspoon salt. Pour the boiling stock over the couscous. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and leave for about 10 minutes.
Then add the butter and fluff up the couscous with a fork until the butter melts in. Cover again and leave somewhere warm.

To serve, spoon couscous into a deep plate or bowl. Stir the harissa and preserved lemon into the vegetables; taste and add salt if needed. Spoon the vegetables onto the center of the couscous. Finish with plenty of cilantro leaves.

name: These
intro: These two dishes are by no means the same, but they are prepared in such similar ways that it makes sense to share one overarching vegan alternative. The main diﬀerence between the two dishes is that while isi ewu contains goat head and brains, nkwobi contains chopped cow feet. The meat substitute I recommend for this dish is seitan (e.g. VChunks - see page 29) because it has the structure and texture required to make this work. In place of that, you can also use mushrooms.

ingredients.item: [approx. 300g] seitan or mushrooms (cut into large chunks)
ground black pepper or cameroon pepper
red onion (half roughly chopped; half sliced into rings)

method: Place the seitan or mushrooms in a pot and cover with water. Season with 1 vegetable stock cube, a pinch of salt and roughly chopped onions. Cook over high heat for 10 minutes. Remove the seitan/mushrooms from the broth and set aside. The broth is not needed and can be repurposed in another recipe.

Add the palm oil to another pot but do not place on the heat yet. Add the baking soda mixture and stir continuously until the oil turns paler in colour. Add the ehuru, black pepper/cameroon pepper, vegetable stock cube, seaweed flakes and salt to taste. Stir until well combined. Add the ugba and the cooked seitan/mushrooms and mix well to combine.
Place the pot on medium-low heat for 5 minutes to warm it through. Serve with a garnish of shredded utazi leaves and onion slices.

name: Thessaly Almond Cookies
method: In a mixing bowl, beat the sugars, butter, cocoa and extracts until creamy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine the baking soda and flour.
Gradually add to sugar mixture.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls 2 inch apart onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake at 380 degrees F for 8-10 minutes or until edges are firm.
Remove to wire racks to cool.

name: Thick and Glossy Fudge Frosting
intro: While cocoa powder is bitter on its own, when used properly, it provides a strong chocolate flavor. Plus, in unsweetened cocoa powder seventy-five to eighty-five percent of the cocoa butter has been removed, making cocoa a valuable asset to a health-conscious chocolate chef. You’ll want to swirl this glossy frosting thickly on any of the cupcakes in Chapter Three.

ingredients.item: boiling water, plus more as needed to adjust final consistency
pure maple syrup, Grade B or dark amber, or agave syrup
/ 27 grams organic whole cane sugar, ground in a blender until powdered
mild tasting extra-virgin olive oil or coconut oil, melted or solid

method: Sift the cocoa powder into a skillet or shallow 8 to 9-inch / 20 to 23-cm saucepan. Pour the boiling water and maple syrup over the cocoa and whisk to dissolve. Set aside for 10 minutes to allow the cocoa to bloom.

Add the granulated and whole cane sugars, oil, and salt to the skillet. Cook over low heat, whisking frequently, until wisps of steam are visible. Be sure to stir the bottom to keep the cocoa from burning. Cook for 2 minutes, adjusting the heat as needed to keep the chocolate steaming, and stirring frequently.

Raise the heat slightly, just enough so that the frosting bubbles slowly, and cook for 30 seconds, until the frosting is shiny and smooth and thick enough to spread. Immediately remove the pan from the heat, and add the vanilla and chocolate extracts, if using.

Check the final consistency of the frosting: Refrigerate a tablespoon of frosting in a small dish for 10 minutes. After chilling, the frosting should be thick and fudgy but still easy to spread. If it is too thick, add additional boiling water, a little at a time, and repeat the test. If no adjustment is needed, cool to room temperature in the skillet. It is ready to use as soon as it has cooled.

name: Thick Fudge Sauce
intro: Deep, dark, thick fudge sauce was a staple in my refrigerator during my pre-vegan days—and it still is, now that I’ve got this recipe to use! I dip bananas into it, spread it on bread, and eat it straight off a spoon. Heat the sauce until it is liquid (it will still be thick) and pour over ice cream, puddings, or whatever you fancy. This sauce tastes best warm.

ingredients.item: to 3 tablespoons / 30 to 45 ml pure maple syrup, Grade B or dark amber

method: Sift the cocoa into a heavy-bottomed skillet, preferably one with sloping sides. Whisk until the cocoa is free of lumps. Add the salt. Pour the water over the cocoa. Use a silicone spatula to mix to a paste.

Wait 5 minutes, then cook the mixture over medium-low heat for 1 minute, whisking frequently, until wisps of steam appear on the surface and a few small bubbles form around the sides. It is important to stir the bottom and sides so that the cocoa does not burn while it cooks and thickens; adjust the heat as necessary. The mixture may become lumpy as it cooks but will smooth out as you whisk.
Add the granulated sugar, maple syrup, and olive oil. Continue to cook, whisking constantly until the mixture boils. Immediately reduce the heat to low and whisk for 30 seconds.
Remove the saucepan from the heat. Add the vanilla and whisk slowly until the bubbling stops.
Cool the sauce to room temperature in the skillet, whisking a few times as it cools. Use immediately, or pour it into a container, let it come to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate.

name: Thick Noodle Soup

ingredients.item: medium chayote, peeled and cut into 1½-inch (4 cm) cubes
medium carrot, peeled and cut into 1½-inch (4 cm) cubes
daikon radish (about 4 inches/10 cm), cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) rounds
medium corncob, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) rounds
package (15 ounces/425 g) fresh bánh canh noodles (see Note)
OR (make your own noodles) 2 cups (320 g) rice flour, plus more for dusting
mushrooms (shiitake, straw, white beech, or similar), stems trimmed and sliced
sponge gourd, peeled and cut into half-moon slices
vegan fish sauce or soy sauce
Vietnamese mint, finely chopped, for garnish
freshly ground black pepper, for garnish

method: Add the water, chayote, carrot, daikon radish, corn, and 1 teaspoon of salt to a large saucepan, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until vegetables have lost their sweet flavor (about 1 hour).

If using store-bought noodles, simply follow the directions on the package. To make your own, combine the rice flour, tapioca starch, and 1 teaspoon of salt in a large bowl. Make a hole in the center, carefully pour in boiling water, and mix with a spatula until water is fully incorporated (3 to 5 minutes).

When it is cool enough to handle, either knead the dough in a stand mixer using a dough hook for 10 minutes on medium speed or with your hands until it is soft and non-sticky. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest for about 30 minutes.
Sprinkle some flour on a work surface and, using a rolling pin, roll out the dough until it is about ¼ inch (6 mm) thick. Cut into 3-inch (7.5 cm) noodle strips.

Fill a large saucepan halfway with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Add 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil and the homemade noodles and cook until al dente and the noodles float to the surface (about 5 minutes). Dump into a colander and rinse under cold water to remove excess starch.

Heat ¼ cup (60 mL) of vegetable oil in a small skillet over medium-low heat. When hot, add the tofu and cook until golden brown on all sides (10 to 15 minutes). Transfer the tofu to a cooling rack or paper towel–lined plate to drain. When cool, cut into ½-inch (1 cm) thick slices.

In a medium skillet, heat annatto oil over medium-low heat. When hot, add leek and cook and stir until fragrant and slightly golden (about 1 minute). Add mushrooms, sponge gourd, and fried tofu slices. Season with vegan fish sauce and cook and stir until mushrooms and sponge gourd are tender (about 3 minutes). Remove from heat.
Fill a large serving bowl halfway with cooked noodles and top with tofu, mushrooms, and sponge gourd. Ladle hot broth over the top and garnish with chopped Vietnamese mint and ground pepper.

name: Thin Scaloppine
intro: I like to serve this dish with halved cherry tomatoes and some rocket scattered over the top for both taste and colour.
method: Get your butcher to cut the scaloppine quite thick and then, with a meat tenderiser, flatten them into a round shape, as big as a plate. Dust the surface of the meat with a little flour, coat with some beaten egg, then press the meat into the breadcrumbs.

Melt the butter in a frying pan and add the oil and sage leaves. When the butter foams, cook the scaloppine well on both sides until golden. Season with salt and pepper, and serve with a few wedges of lemon, or add some rocket and cherry tomatoes.

name: Three-Color Sticky Rice

ingredients.item: sticky rice, rinsed, soaked for 4 to 8 hours, and drained
gấc fruit seeds with aril or 2 ounces (56 g) gấc fruit paste (see Note)
sticky rice, rinsed, soaked for 4 to 8 hours, and drained
recipe mashed mung beans (make them with an additional ¼ cup/50 g peeled split mung beans and an additional ¼ cup/60 ml water)

method: In a blender, combine the chopped pandan leaves and water and pulse until smooth. Soak sticky rice in pandan juice for 4 to 6 hours. Drain in a colander, shake off excess water, and set aside.

In a large bowl, combine gấc seeds with aril or gấc paste and cooking wine (if using). Wearing plastic gloves, mix vigorously to remove pulps and arils from the stones, then discard the stones (skip this last part if you used the paste). Add soaked rice and salt to the bowl and toss well until coated red.

Fill a large pot that can hold an 8- to-10-inch (20 to 25 cm) steamer basket with water until it is 1 inch (2.5 cm) below the base of the basket, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Line steamer basket with a banana leaf or piece of parchment paper to prevent rice from falling through the grates and sticking. Spread the red and green rice evenly, side by side in the steamer basket, and then poke a few holes through the layer. Wrap the steamer lid in a kitchen towel and tie the corners over the handle to absorb excess steam and prevent it dropping in the rice. Cover the steamer basket and place it on top of the boiling pot. Steam until the rice is tender, sticky, slightly chewy, and no longer opaque (35 to 40 minutes).

In a small bowl, mix coconut milk, salt, and ¼ cup (50 g) of sugar. Stir to dissolve. During the last 15 minutes of steaming, drizzle one-third of the coconut milk mixture over the rice. Cover and steam for 5 minutes. Repeat three more times until all the coconut milk mixture is gone.
In a medium bowl, mix mashed mung beans with 2 tablespoons of sugar until combined.

Place a sticky rice mold on a flat surface with the patterned side facedown. Fill the mold one-third full with red or green sticky rice and spread in an even layer. Continue with a similar amount of mashed mung beans, and then another layer of the remaining color of sticky rice. Compress with the lid of the mold to form into a sticky rice cake, and then immediately unmold to reveal the beauty of three-color sticky rice.

name: Three-Layer Tacos with Kale Slaw
intro: You’ll want taco night every night of the week with these overflowing tacos. The tofu gets marinated with the pinto beans, and a spicy-sweet slaw serves as a topping.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into ½-inch chunks
15-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, chopped finely
plus 2 tablespoons unsweetened dairy-free milk, divided
15-ounce cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle pepper in adobo sauce (about 2 peppers), chopped
white corn taco shells or tortillas, or your favorite
Favorite toppings: spinach, lettuce, black olives, lime, avocado, peppers
diced red bell pepper (about one small pepper)
broccoli, inner stalks cut into cubes and florets cut into bites
canned black beans, drained and rinsed
sweet potato, peeled and chopped into bite-size pieces
dry white wine, such as chardonnay
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
small head cauliflower, cut into florets
small head broccoli, cut into florets
cooked black beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, chopped small, and 1 tablespoon adobo sauce
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
Steamed Seitan Chipotle Links, torn into bite-size pieces (page 284)
15-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into ½-inch cubes
Slow Cooker Versatile Seitan Balls, chopped (page 279)
Slow Cooker Versatile Seitan Balls, cubed (page 279)
15-ounce cans black beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, finely chopped
Additional toppings, such as more salsa, avocado or guacamole, and black olives
whole wheat or sprouted grain tortillas
Steamed Seitan Smoky Nuggets (page 283), cut into bite-size pieces if necessary
broccoli, stems peeled and diced, florets cut into bite-size pieces
cobs of corn, kernels cut from the cob
hot sauce, such as Tabasco (omit if you don’t like spicy; you can put it on the table instead)
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cubed
15-ounce cans black beans, drained and rinsed

method: Mix the taco seasoning and tamari in a small bowl. Set aside.
Add the tofu to the tamari mix and toss. Marinate while working on the bean mixture and slaw.
Add the beans, onion, tomatoes, salt, pepper, and parsley to a small bowl. Toss and set aside to meld.

Add the kale to a medium bowl and add the lemon juice. Massage the kale with your hands to soften it up. Add both cabbages, the carrots, mayonnaise, lime juice, maple syrup, and chili in adobo sauce. Mix well.
Assemble the tacos by layering the shells with the bean mixture, tofu, and finally the slaw.

name: Tiramisu

ingredients.item: cocoa powder plus cocoa powder to sprinkle on top.

method: Boil ¼ cup water. In the meantime, in a bowl that could fit if you place it on top of the pot,( because you will be double bowling the eggs in a minute,) with an electric mixer, beat eggs and sugar for a minute. Transfer bowl to pot of boiling water…they call this bagnomaria in Italian. Beat for 3 minutes then remove from heat. Mix for an additional 5 minutes. Add Kahlua and mascarpone and beat for a minute or until well blended. Scrape down sides with rubber spatula. In a separate bowl, beat heavy cream until light and fluffy. Gently fold cream into the egg mixture. Cover with plastic and refrigerate for an hour. Brew espresso coffee and transfer to a bowl. Add Kahlua, brown sugar, and cocoa powder, mix well. Let mixture cool. Soak ladyfingers in coffee mixture, not too much or they will fall apart. Layer on the bottom of an 8-inch casserole dish until you have covered the bottom. Spread a layer of cream on top of the layer of ladyfingers. Try to divide the mixture evenly between the layers. Resume the next layer as you did the first, and then add the remaining cream. Sprinkle with cocoa powder, and refrigerate for an hour. Serves 4. Olé

name: Tiropsomo
method: Put all the ingredients, except the oils for oiling and frying and the cheeses, in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. Mix on medium-low speed for 8 minutes. Add the cheeses and mix for a further 2 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a large bowl lightly brushed with olive oil and cover tightly with clingfilm. Leave to stand in a warm place for an hour.
Cut the dough into pieces of about 40–50g (1½–1¾oz) each and roll them lightly with your hands into balls. Then using a rolling pin, flatten each ball into a round 1–1.5cm (½–5∕8 inch) thick.

Fill a large, deep saucepan no more than halfway with sunflower oil and heat to 170°C (340°F). Deep-fry the little breads, as many as will fit comfortably in your pan at a time without overcrowding it, for 1–3 minutes until golden on both sides. Drain and place on a plate lined with kitchen paper to soak up the excess oil.
Alternatively, shape the dough into larger breads, 80–100g (3–3½oz) each, and bake on 2 baking trays in an oven preheated to 190°C (375°F), Gas Mark 5, for 20 minutes.
Serve the breads warm or at room temperature.

name: Titi’s Lasagna for Dad
intro: Remove the tofu from the package and, using two paper towels, gently squeeze the extra water from the tofu block. Break up the tofu, place it in a blender and pulse about three times until you get big crumbles.
method: My dad was an unhappy man, and I don’t have the best memories of him. My mom separated from him when I was seven, and he was in and out of my life briefly until he just stopped showing up. Years passed, and in 2011, he reached out because he was in the hospital and needed heart surgery. I was happy to hear that he wanted my siblings and me to visit him, but I was also sad because of the awful memories I had of him and the fact he just disappeared from my life. Although I wanted to hate him, I just couldn’t.

My siblings and I went to Lebanon Hospital to see him for the first time in years. I couldn’t believe he and I were together again, although he wasn’t in great shape and it was a vulnerable moment for him. We all sat down, and I tried my hardest to hold back my tears. But when my sister sat down, she immediately started with the waterworks, and I couldn’t hold it in anymore and started to cry as well. He told us to stop crying and that everything was okay, but I think we were crying because, although he had been mean to us, we had missed him and still loved him.

After that day, we would visit him occasionally. I remember he texted me and told me to bring him lasagna. I told my mom and she said that was his favorite dish. I don’t think I ever brought it for him, though. I think I forgot, or we just stopped seeing him again for a while. He was too prideful to reach out to us, and I was too busy living my life. My dad stopped contacting us after some years. Then, in 2020, I was in the nail salon when the news came on and reported Kobe Bryant had died. I wasn’t a huge basketball fan, but his death hurt me, and I felt incredibly sad for a while. It impacted me and then I started to think of my dad. Weeks went by, and it was still heavy on my heart. I was in my sister’s room, and I casually asked her whether she has spoken to Dad and she replied, “No, I haven’t; I forgot where he was staying.” I told her I knew where he was, and we Googled his number the next day and called. He was at a rehab facility; when we phoned, they broke the bad news to us that he was extremely sick. No one had called us because they didn’t have our contact information. I remember feeling so angry. My sister and I called the hospital he was staying in for the doctor to tell us he had been in the ICU for 22 days and he was unconscious and not responding. My sister and I rushed home to get ready, and five minutes before we left for the hospital, they called us back to tell us he didn’t make it. I felt so much guilt and so much pain. February 14, 2020, my dad was gone. I wished for so many things to be different, but I had to stay strong for my family. As we were leaving, I’ll never forget what the nurse told me; she said, “He waited for you.” I truly believe he did, and he intentionally passed on Valentine’s Day to remind me how much he loved me, as I like to think.

My dad’s love for lasagna makes me think of Titi Mildred’s lasagna. She is always asked to make it for family gatherings or events because it is that good. Even if she doesn’t go to the event, we ask that she make the lasagna and we pick it up from her. Titi Mildred still hasn’t shared her secret with me, but she gave me a few hints about what she does, so I ran with that information and re-created my best vegan version of it. It still doesn’t quite compare, but I think I am close. The lasagna is creamy, savory, saucy and herby. Every bite is an explosion of flavor. I wish I could have brought my dad a piece of Titi’s lasagna. He would have loved it just as much as I do.

Add your nutritional yeast, apple cider vinegar, grapeseed oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, Italian seasoning and nondairy milk to the blender. Blend everything together until smooth, then set aside.
In a pot over medium heat, heat your olive oil, then add your white onion and garlic and cook until tender, about 4 minutes.

Add your Beyond Meat sausage and beef and break them down until you get crumbles. Mix in your tomato paste, stirring until the sauce turns red and there are no tomato paste clumps left. Gradually add the crushed tomato and tomato sauce while stirring.

Follow that with the cane sugar, fennel seeds, oregano, parsley, salt, pepper and basil, and combine thoroughly. Lower the heat to low and let the sauce simmer for 15 minutes for the flavors to settle in.

In a large baking dish, lay all the lasagna noodles on the bottom of the dish. Submerge the noodles in hot water and let them sit for about 30 minutes. (Hot water from the tap is fine for this—it doesn’t need to be boiling.) This softens the noodles a bit before assembling and baking. It also prevents them from absorbing all the sauce.
Remove the water and noodles from the dish, draining the noodles of the water and placing them on a plate. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Spread ¼ cup (60 ml) of meat sauce on the bottom of the baking dish, covering the bottom completely. Lay down four to five lasagna noodles, covering the layer of meat sauce evenly. Spread a layer of tofu ricotta on top of the noodles, then spread another layer of meat sauce and cover with another layer of lasagna noodles.

Repeat by spreading a layer of tofu ricotta on top of the noodles, then a layer of meat sauce. Top the meat sauce with a handful of the vegan mozzarella cheese all over and cover with another layer of lasagna noodles. Repeat one more time. When you get to the very top, add some meat sauce, a few dollops of tofu ricotta and another handful of the mozzarella.
Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 35 minutes. Then, remove the foil and bake for an additional 10 minutes to brown up the cheese a bit.
Take the lasagna out the oven and get ready to serve. ¡Buen provecho!

name: To the Power of Four Overnight Oats
intro: If you haven’t had overnight oats before, then here is a fantastic recipe that will make you a believer. It’s simple to the nth degree and features everyone’s favorite ingredients.

ingredients.item: 15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
ground chia seeds or chia seeds, divided
ground chia seeds or chia seeds
frozen banana, 4 slices reserved for topping
almond milk or other dairy-free milk
plus 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, divided
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and crumbled
Slow Cooker Maple Breakfast Links, sliced thick (page 276)
15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
peeled and sliced apples (I like them kind of thick)
almond milk or other dairy-free milk
Slow Cooker Maple Breakfast Links, sliced (page 276)
15-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
flour tortillas, 8 to 10 inches in diameter

name: Toasted Protein Mushroom Rolls
intro: Here’s something that you probably haven’t seen before. Roll some bread flat, spread with filling, roll up, and bake. Whoa!

ingredients.item: baby spinach, with stems chopped off
seitan (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
tempeh, diced very small, or pulsed small
15-ounce can chickpeas, drained (save the liquid to use as aquafaba) and rinsed

method: Add cashews, milk, lemon juice, salt, and pepper to a food processor. Process until smooth.
Clean mushrooms and finely chop.
Heat 1 tablespoon butter over medium-high heat in a small skillet. Add chopped mushrooms and sauté for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and add the cashew mixture and hempseed. Stir well.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Cut crusts off of the bread and leave in a square shape. Roll each square thin with a rolling pin. You will be rolling up these squares. Spread 1 tablespoon mushroom mixture onto each square and roll up.
Melt remaining butter.
Cut rolls in half and roll in melted butter. Place rolls on cookie sheets and bake for 8 minutes or until browned.

name: Tofu and haricots verts with chraimeh sauce
intro: also be frozen and kept for 1 month), so make double or triple the quantities. It

ingredients.item: oz/400g firm tofu, cut into 1-inch/2½cm cubes and patted dry salt
caraway seeds, lightly toasted and crushed in a pestle and mortar
limes: juice 1 to get 1 tbsp and cut the other into 4 wedges, to serve salt
