name: Two bean and two lime salad
intro: you serve. It will keep for up to 6 hours in the fridge. If you can’t get hold of fresh

ingredients.item: large kaffir lime leaves (fresh or frozen), stems removed
large limes:  nely zest to get 1½ tsp, then juice to get 2 tbsp
green chiles, seeded and thinly sliced salt

method: Roll up all the kaffir leaves into a thick cigar shape. Slice as thinly as possible, then  nely chop the strips. Place in the bowl of a food processor with the lime zest, 1 cup/20g of cilantro, the mint, garlic, olive oil, chile, and ½ tsp of salt. Blitz until smooth, then set aside.

Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil and add the green beans. Blanch for 3 minutes, then add the edamame and cook for 1 minute. Drain all together, refresh under cold water, and set aside to dry.
Spoon the lime paste over the beans, add the lime juice, and stir to combine.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds, along with the remaining ½ cup/5g of cilantro, and serve at once.
Mushrooms and chestnuts with za’atar

These are lovely as an autumn or festive side. They are also great for breakfast, served with scrambled eggs. Use any mushrooms—or a mix of mushrooms— depending on what you see. Just keep the net weight the same. If you’ve got large shallots lying around, they are ne to use—just cut them in half or even into quarters.
If you want to get ahead, prepare this up to 4 hours in advance—just place everything on the baking sheet, minus the salt and pepper, ready to be seasoned before roasting.

name: Two-potato vindaloo
intro: Here’s a great recipe you can make heaps of and keep for a few days. It only gets better! As always, thick cool yogurt will make an excellent condiment.

ingredients.item: ripe tomatoes, peeled and roughly chopped
peeled waxy potatoes, cut into 1-inch dice
small red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch dice
peeled sweet potatoes, cut into 1-inch dice
mint or cilantro leaves, to serve

method: Dry-roast the cardamom pods and cumin and coriander seeds in a small frying pan over medium heat until they begin to pop. Transfer to a mortar and pestle and add the cloves. Work to a fine powder, removing and discarding the cardamom pods once the seeds are released. Add the turmeric, paprika and cinnamon and set aside.

Heat up the oil in a large heavy-based pot. Add the shallots with the mustard and fenugreek seeds, and sauté on a medium–low heat for 8 minutes, or until the shallots brown. Stir in the spice mix, curry leaves, ginger and chile and cook for a further 3 minutes. Next, add the tomatoes, vinegar, water, sugar and some salt. Bring to the boil, then leave to simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.

Add the potatoes and bell peppers and simmer for another 20 minutes. For the last stage, add the sweet potatoes. Make sure all the vegetables are just immersed in the sauce (add more water if needed) and continue cooking, covered, for about 40 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
Remove the lid and leave to bubble away for about 10 minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce. Serve hot, with plain rice and garnished with herbs.

name: Tzatziki Chicken
method: Blend the first six ingredients with the gravy; chill in the fridge until
served.
Mix the flour, spice, seasoning, and baking powder in such a small
Mix the egg and milk in that dish. Pound the chicken breasts with a
half-inch meat mallet thickness.
To dust all ends, dip in the flour mixture; shake off the residue. Roll in
the beaten egg, then the starch mixture again.
Heat oil over moderate heat in a large pan.
Cook the chicken until the juices are golden brown and transparent, 5-
7 minutes on either side.
Serve with liquid and lime wedges if needed.

name: Tzulamas

ingredients.item: sweet red wine, such as Mavrodaphne or sweet Marsala
Aleppo pepper or pinch of crushed red pepper flakes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
). Flatten the cord with the tines of a fork to prevent it from sticking up, or it will burn during baking. Brush the top generously with the milk.

method: In a large, deep skillet, heat the oil or butter and sauté the livers over medium heat until firm, about 4 minutes. Add the pork and sauté for 4 minutes more. Add the wine, currants, cinnamon sticks and Aleppo pepper or pepper flakes, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the pork is no longer pink. Remove from the heat and stir in the rice, 1 cup of the stock, the almonds, pistachios, sugar, cinnamon and salt and pepper to taste. Let cool. Remove the cinnamon sticks.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Oil or butter a 13-x-9- inch baking dish.

If using phyllo, divide the dough into 4 pieces and fit 2 sheets into the bottom and up the sides of the dish, brushing each sheet with oil or butter, and trim to a 1-inch overhang. Add the filling, smoothing it with a spatula, and pour the remaining 1 cup stock over it. Cover with the remaining 2 sheets phyllo, brushing each with oil or butter. Fold the overhanging bottom crust up over the top crust and pinch the top edges together to seal, crimping them to make a neat cord around the edge of the pie (see illustrations). Flatten the cord with the tines of a fork to prevent it from sticking up, or it will burn during baking. Brush the top generously with the milk.

If using puff pastry, divide into 3 portions. Cover 1 piece with plastic wrap. Briefly knead the other 2 pieces together, then roll out on a lightly floured surface. Fit 1 sheet of pastry into the dish, and trim to a 1-inch overhang. Add the filling, smoothing the top with a spatula, and pour the remaining 1 cup stock over it. Cover with the other sheet. Pinch the two edges together, turn them inward and press to seal. Brush the top generously with milk.

Bake for 15 minutes, sprinkling the top of the pie 8 to 10 times with water. Bake for 10 minutes more, then reduce the oven temperature to 350°F and bake for 30 to 40 minutes more, or until golden brown. Check often, and if the pastry puffs up, prick it in several places with a knife. If the top browns too quickly, cover it loosely with aluminum foil. Turn off the oven, but leave the pie in the oven for 10 minutes more.
Let the pie cool on a rack for 15 minutes then sprinkle with confectioners’ sugar and cinnamon and serve.

name: Udon Noodles With Fried Eggplant, Walnut, And Miso

ingredients.item: green onions, white and green parts
1⅓-inch/3.5-cm piece (about 1 oz/25 g), peeled fresh ginger, cut into very fine matchsticks
small eggplants (about 1 lb/500 g) about 1 cup/250 ml sunflower oil, plus 1 tablespoon
cups/120 g walnuts, lightly toasted and coarsely chopped
tbsp/50 g sweet white miso paste
cup/150 ml vegetarian dashi or vegetable stock from cube
cucumber, unpeeled, cored and cut into very fine strips (5 oz/150 g) salt

method: Cut each green onion into 2-inch/5-cm lengths. Slice each length in two, from top to bottom, and then cut each half into long strips, as thinly as you can.
Place the onions and two-fifths of the ginger in a bowl of iced water and put in the fridge.

Use a vegetable peeler to peel off 4 or 5 strips of skin from the eggplants, from top to bottom, so you are left with a striped pattern. Slice the eggplants into disks 1-inch/2.5 cm-thick and then cut each disk into quarters. Pour the
1 cup/250 ml sunflower oil into a saucepan and place over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the eggplant pieces in small batches and deep-fry for about 4 minutes, until they turn golden and cook through. Transfer to a colander to drain and sprinkle with a little salt.
Place the shallots and the remaining 1 tablespoon sunflower oil in a large sauté pan and sauté over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until they soften.
Add the remaining ginger and the garlic and cook over low heat for 5 minutes. Add the walnuts and fried eggplant pieces and set aside.
Whisk together the miso, dashi, mirin, soy sauce, sugar, and sake in a small bowl. Add to the walnuts and eggplants.

Cook the noodles as instructed on the package. While you do this, heat up the eggplant and walnut sauce, allowing some evaporation so the sauce thickens a little but not much. Serve individual portions of hot noodles, topped in the center with the eggplant and walnut sauce. Drain and pat dry the green onion and ginger and sprinkle these on top, along with the cucumber.

name: Ugba Salad
intro: Also known as oil bean salad, this dish is popular in the eastern parts of Nigeria, particularly amongst the Igbo. The shredded and fermented oil bean seeds have an umami taste. If you live outside of Nigeria, it is possible to find ugba from specialised African food shops or from online retailers. Sometimes it is also labelled as ukpaka. If possible, go with the unsalted version so that you can control the amount of saltiness in the dish.

ingredients.item: crushed chilli flakes or cameroon pepper
1/2 teaspoon ground Uziza seed or black peppercorns
1/4 cup shredded ukazi leaves or shredded spinach

method: Add the palm oil and baking soda mixture to a mixing bowl and whisk continuously until well combined and emulsified. Add the crushed chilli flakes, ehuru (or nutmeg) and ground Uziza (or peppercorn). Mix well to combine, then add the ugba and stir to coat evenly.
Add the sliced onions, shredded ukazi (or spinach) and garden egg to garnish.

name: Ukpo Ogede
intro: Building on the classic Moin Moin (page 158), here we have a snack or light meal that is made in a similar way but which features the wonderfully versatile plantain! These “steamed plantain puddings” are a great way to showcase plantains. It’s a perfect balance of sweet, savoury and spicy, which your taste buds will thank you for. Although they are traditionally steamed in uma leaves, you can use small ramekins instead.

ingredients.item: 1/2 cup plantain flour or fine cornmeal
uma leaves or banana leaves for steaming (optional)

method: Place the water, ripe plantains, onion and scotch bonnet in a food blender or food processor and blend until you have a smooth batter.
Transfer the batter to a mixing bowl and add the plantain flour/cornmeal, palm oil and salt. Mix well to combine.

Place the leaf parcels or ramekins into a steamer and steam over medium-low heat for 45 minutes. Ensure that the parcels are laid flat. Halfway through the cooking time, check that the water in the steamer has not dried up during the cooking time.

name: Ukwa (African Breadfruit Porridge)
intro: The star of this flavourful and nutritious Igbo dish is ukwa, or African breadfruit. If using dried ukwa, be sure to soak it overnight before cooking, otherwise you can skip the soaking step. The porridge is wonderfully savoury with a hint of spice and sweetness. Ukwa is delicious when cooked plain with a pinch of salt but the additional ingredients included here take it to the next level.

ingredients.item: 1/2 cup bitter leaves (washed, drained and chopped)
vegetable stock cube Salt to taste

method: Wash/rinse the pre-soaked ukwa several times in a colander to remove any grit or dirt.

Place the ukwa, chopped onions, 3 cups of water and baking soda in a large pot. Bring to a boil then cook covered for 45 minutes over medium heat until the ukwa is tender. Check halfway through the cooking time and add extra water if needed.
Once the ukwa is tender, add the palm oil, scotch bonnet chilli, bitter leaves, maize/corn, mushrooms, vegetable stock and salt to taste. Stir and cook for 10 minutes.

name: Ulli Theeyal
intro: A Kerala speciality, this curry has a soupy consistency. Tiny Madras onions bob in a delicious gravy of red chillies, tamarind and fresh coconut.
method: In a pan, heat 1 tbsp of the coconut oil and add 10 curry leaves and the red chillies. Once they begin to crackle, add the coriander seeds. Add the turmeric powder and stir fry it for 2 minutes on medium flame.
Add the coconut and continue stirring for 7-8 minutes. Blend this mixture into a smooth paste. If the mixture is too dry, add a little coconut water.

In another pan, heat 2 tbsp of the coconut oil and add the Madras onions to it. Fry until the onions turn golden brown. Add the tamarind paste followed by the coriander– coconut paste. Add 1 cup of water and allow the dish to simmer on medium flame.
In another pan, heat 1 tbsp of the oil and add the mustard seeds and split black gram. Once they begin to crackle, add the remaining curry leaves and fry for 30 seconds.
Add the tempering to the Madras onions mixture and stir well. Adjust the seasoning and serve hot.

name: Ultimate Vegan Burrito
method: Remove stems from mushroom caps; cut into slices.
Slice bell pepper and red onion.
Take a skillet, and heat oil over the medium heat.
Cook veggies for almost 6-7 minutes.
Put black beans, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, paprika, lime
juice, kosher salt, and some water. Cook until liquid evaporates.
Add kosher salt to the mashed avocado.
To assemble tortilla, put 1/2 cup of rice on it. Top with the bean
mixture, avocado, and vegetable.
Fold in all sides of burritos.
Cut them, and serve.

name: Ultimate Veggie Wrap with Kale Pesto
intro: Pretty in green on the inside and out. Tender broccoli and fresh veggie layers add to the flavorful kale pesto before you roll these up for your first bite.

ingredients.item: raw cashews, soaked at least 2 hours
sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil, drained (save the oil)
oil or reserved oil from the sun-dried tomatoes
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and crumbled
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into 1-inch cubes
sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil, drained (save the oil)
oil or reserved oil from the sun-dried tomatoes
Slow Cooker Maple Breakfast Links, sliced (page 276)
vegan mayonnaise or spread of your choice
seitan, crumbled (Slow Cooker Log for Thin Slices and Crumbles, page 280)
small potato, to equal about ½ cup mashed potato
carrot, finely chopped in a processor
chia seeds or ground chia seeds
ear of corn, kernels cut from the cob, or 1 8-ounce can corn, drained
28-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
Condiments and toppings of your choice
Toppings and condiments: lettuce, tomatoes, red onion, mustard, dairy-free spicy mayo
15-ounce cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed
vegan mayonnaise (add another tablespoon if you like it better that way)
Dijon mustard (add another tablespoon if desired)
slices whole wheat bread or sprouted grain bread
Steamed Seitan Smoky Nuggets, sliced thick (page 283)
baby spinach, chopped, with the long stems cut away and discarded
raw cashews, soaked 1 hour and drained
15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
sprouted grain English muffins, sliced open
Condiments of your choice, such as dairy-free chipotle mayo and horseradish mustard

method: Place the cashews, kale, garlic, and salt in a small food processor. Process for about 30 seconds. Add the nutritional yeast and oil and process a few more seconds until well blended. Set aside.
Add water to a medium saucepan with a steamer insert and bring to a boil. Add the broccoli to the insert and steam over boiling water for 10 minutes. Remove from steamer and set aside.

Lay out the spinach tortillas. Divide the kale pesto between the two tortillas and spread evenly, leaving about 1 inch around all edges. Divide the remaining ingredients in half and lay out each half next to each other and down the length of each tortilla.
Start to roll up snugly, without tearing the tortilla. Cut each tortilla in half and serve.

name: Umami Garlic Noodles with Shiitake Mushroom
intro: A cult favorite among Viet Americans, buttery garlic noodles are addictively good, but their garlicky flavor can linger the morning after. You don’t have to worry about that with this recipe. To prevent the garlic from ruining a date night (and from burning during cooking), let it hang out for a few minutes in a little water and then gently cook it.

ingredients.item: large garlic cloves, minced or put through a press
dried Chinese wheat noodles or Japanese ramen
MSG, scant ½ teaspoon chicken stock base, or 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast flakes
fresh shiitake mushroom or cremini mushrooms, sliced ⅛ to ¼ inch thick, stems included

method: Fill a large pot with 4 quarts water and bring to a boil.

Meanwhile, put the garlic in a small cup or dish and add about 1 tablespoon water to just barely cover. Set aside and expect the garlic to absorb most of the water; there is no need to drain it before adding later.

After the pot comes to a boil, add the noodles and 2 teaspoons salt. Boil the noodles until just chewy-firm; they’ll soften more later. Ladle out ¾ cup of the cooking liquid. Drain the noodles in a colander, rinse with cool water, and set aside. In a small bowl, whisk together the oyster sauce, fish sauce, cornstarch, MSG, sugar, and reserved cooking water. Set aside.

If the pot that you cooked the noodles in is wide enough to comfortably sauté the mushrooms, set it over medium-high heat and melt 2 tablespoons of the butter; if not, use a large skillet. Add the mushrooms, season with 2 or 3 pinches of salt and pepper, and cook, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the mushrooms start to brown. Turn off the heat and transfer the mushrooms to a plate or bowl.

Return the pot to the hot burner. To prevent scorching, keep the heat off as you add the remaining 2 tablespoons butter, the shallot, and garlic. As the butter melts and sizzles, turn the heat to medium-low and cook, stirring frequently, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the garlic is fragrant and some pieces are golden. Add the seasoned cooking water and mushrooms, stir, and increase the heat slightly.

When the sauce starts bubbling, add the noodles. Using tongs and a spoon, combine and coat the noodles in sauce. If the dish looks too thick or tastes too salty, add a tiny splash of water. Turn off the heat and let rest for a minute.
Serve the noodles in individual pasta bowls.

name: Unstuffed Cabbage Soup
intro: One of the most delicious stuffed dishes cooked across the region is stuffed cabbage. The cabbage is stuffed with a mixture of rice, ground beef, and copious amounts of garlic, then simmered in a lemony broth until the cabbage melts in your mouth. But stuffing and rolling leaf after leaf is a labor of love. This soup is how I replicate the flavors of stuffed cabbage but in a fraction of the time. It’s hearty, vibrant, and nutritious, perfect for a cold winter night. Feel free to go wild with the garlic, lemon, and mint quantities—they are the magic trio!

ingredients.item: Cloves from 2 heads garlic, peeled and finely chopped
kosher salt, plus more if needed
large head green cabbage, roughly chopped (see Note)
short-grain rice, rinsed until the water runs clear and drained completely

method: In a large pot over medium heat, combine the oil and garlic and cook, stirring continuously, over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is fragrant and slightly golden.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up into small pieces with a wooden spoon, for 6 to 7 minutes, until browned.
Add the salt, allspice, cinnamon, pepper, and tomato paste, mix everything together, and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes. Add the cabbage and stir to combine.
Add the broth and stir to combine. Cover with the lid and let simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes.

Add the rice, stir, and continue to cook, covered, for 10 minutes. Uncover the pot and add the lemon juice and mint. Stir to combine and taste and adjust the salt if necessary. If the soup is too thick, add a bit of water to thin it out to desired consistency.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with the parsley and mint and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

name: Urad Dal with Coconut and Cilantro

ingredients.item: cups/250 g black urad dal, soaked overnight in plenty of water
cup/60 g clarified butter or ghee
large onion, finely chopped (1⅓ cups/200 g)
4-inch/10-cm piece fresh ginger (2½ oz/75 g), peeled and coarsely grated
green chile, flesh and seeds finely chopped
medium tomatoes, peeled and coarsely chopped (3½ cups/600 g)
lime juice, plus 1 lime, cut into wedges, to serve
cups/100 g coarsely grated fresh coconut
cups/30 g cilantro leaves, coarsely chopped

method: Drain the dal, rinse under cold water, and set aside.

Place the butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. When it starts to sizzle, add the onion and fry for 15 minutes, stirring from time to time, until soft and golden brown. Add the garlic, ginger, chile, and garam masala and fry for another 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Add the tomatoes and cook for a further 4 minutes. Add the dal, 4½ cups/1 liter water, and 1 teaspoon salt.

Turn down the heat to medium and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or so, until the sauce has the consistency of thick soup and the dal is cooked but still holding its shape. Bring to a rapid boil for a few minutes toward the end of cooking if the sauce needs reducing.

Turn the heat down to low, then stir in the coconut cream, lime juice, and black mustard seeds. Remove from the heat and serve, accompanied with the toppings in 3 separate bowls, for diners to sprinkle on top of their portion as they like.

name: Use-It-up Fried Rice
intro: Along with banh mi and tacos, fried rice is another go-to for repurposing leftovers. It’s easy to make a luxurious mound of cơm chiên, as long as you remember a few points: To ensure grains that don’t gum up, use dry-ish, cooked rice. Make the rice up to 5 days ahead, or prepare a fresh batch (see this page) and let it cool completely on a baking sheet.

ingredients.item: cooked long-grain rice, such as white or brown jasmine, at room temperature (or a few minutes out of the fridge)
fat, such as canola oil, peanut oil, coconut oil, rendered lard, or European-style butter
to 1½ cups cooked leftovers, such as meat, seafood, vegetables, tofu, or tempeh (or a combination), cut or broken up into pieces the size of large peas
fish sauce, soy sauce, Bragg Liquid Aminos, or Maggi Seasoning sauce, plus more for serving
green onion, white and green parts, chopped

method: Stir the rice to prevent lumps. Set with the remaining ingredients near the stove—this recipe comes together quickly.

In a large nonstick or carbon-steel skillet over medium-high or high heat, warm 1 tablespoon of the fat. When the fat is nearly shimmering, add the garlic and stir-fry for 10 to 15 seconds, until aromatic. Add the leftovers and cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes to reheat and refresh. Add the rice and stir-fry for about 2 minutes, until warm and slightly revived.

Push the rice to the skillet’s perimeter to create a 4-inch-well in the middle. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon fat to the well, pour in the egg, then pour the fish sauce around the rim of the well (onto the rice). Quickly stir-fry to break up, scramble, and work the golden egg bits into the rice. Add the green onion and cook for 10 to 15 seconds longer, until just wilted. Turn off the heat, taste, and season with salt, if needed.
Transfer the rice to a plate or shallow bowl. Serve with additional fish sauce, soy sauce, or Maggi Seasoning in case diners want an extra-savory punch.

name: Vacalao Guisado
intro: Vacalao guisado is a remake of bacalao guisado (salt fish stew). This dish has seafood notes, saltiness and sauciness. Shredded jackfruit and hearts of palm make the perfect salt fish substitute here.

ingredients.item: cans hearts of palm, drained and rinsed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper

method: Chop your hearts of palm into small pieces, place in a bowl and marinate it in 1 tablespoon (5 g) of the nori furikake.

Bring a medium-sized pot of water to a boil. Add the drained jackfruit to the boiling water and cook for 30 minutes to extract the brine. Remove from the water and pat out the excess liquid with a paper towel. Shred the jackfruit, season it in the remaining tablespoon (5 g) of nori furikake and set it aside.

In a large pot over medium heat, heat your oil and sauté the sofrito, garlic, onion and bell peppers to release the aromatics and soften the onion. Add the tomato sauce, vegetable stock, olive mixture, Sazón, adobo, oregano, the marinated hearts of palm and the jackfruit. Optionally, you can also add a pinch of sugar here to make it a bit less acidic. Cook the stew covered, for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the cilantro in the last 5 minutes, and season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve and enjoy.

name: Vada Pav
intro: These mildly spiced, deep-fried potato burgers are a delicious way to use up leftover mashed potatoes. The mashed potato is first fried with a few complementary spices and herbs, and then formed into large balls that are dipped into a seasoned gram-flour batter. Everything, right up to making the sandwich, can be done ahead of time. At busy restaurants and street stalls, the potato vada are formed and fried earlier in the day and heated through again in hot oil before serving. This is really convenient if you are serving a group of friends. When I tried these at food stalls in India there was always a plate of roasted chillies you could help yourself to for topping your vada pav, making them as mild or spicy as you want. If you really want to treat yourself, spread lots of butter on the buns before grilling!

ingredients.item: green chillies, finely chopped, plus extra to garnish
sifted gram (chickpea) flour, plus extra if needed
Ghee, butter or oil, for browning the buns

method: Boil the potatoes in water for about 10 minutes until fork-tender. Drain and mash.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium–high heat. Add the mustard seeds. When they begin to pop (after about 30 seconds), stir in the turmeric, green chillies, ginger, chilli powder and curry leaves. Move this all around in the pan to flavour the oil, then add the mashed potatoes and mix well. Season with salt and add the coriander (cilantro). Allow to cool slightly, then form into eight lemon-size balls.

Whisk the batter ingredients together, adding enough water slowly to make a thick and smooth batter. The batter should cling to, and coat, the vada. If you find it is too thin, sift in a little more flour.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a large pan. The oil should be deep enough to cover the vada. You are ready to start deep-frying when a piece of potato sizzles immediately when dropped into the hot oil. If you have an oil thermometer, aim for 200°C (390°F). Carefully lower the vada into the oil and fry until crispy brown – about 3–5 minutes should do. Depending on the size of your pan, you may need to cook these in small batches of three or four.

While the vada are frying, brown the buns in another pan in some ghee, butter or oil. When toasted to your liking, spread the mint and coriander sauce over the bun halves. Place a vada on top of the bottom bun and top with tamarind sauce (if using) and one or more roasted chillies if you like it spicy. Add the top bun and serve.

name: Valdostana Soup
intro: This mountain soup is really a meal in itself, which is how it was traditionally served.

ingredients.item: oaf ciabatta bread, thinly sliced and toasted

method: Preheat the oven to 200°C (gas mark 6).
In a large pan heat the chicken stock. Butter six large, ovenproof soup bowls.
Remove the leaves from the Savoy cabbage, cut away any thick stems and cut the leaves into large pieces. Cut the cavolo nero into large pieces.
Rub the toasted ciabatta bread with the garlic clove.

In the bottom of each bowl, put some cabbage and cavolo nero. On top of this place about 3 anchovy fillets then a handful of fontina and Gruyère cheeses. Arrange 1–2 slices of the toasted ciabatta on top. Continue with more layers of cabbage and cavolo nero, anchovies and parmigiano, then finally some ground pepper.

Now fill the bowls to three-quarters with the hot stock (do not fill them too full, as the bread will swell a bit during cooking). Cook them in the oven for about 15–20 minutes. The soup should have a nice golden, crunchy crust on top. Serve immediately.
If you cannot find cavolo nero, substitute with fresh English spinach.

name: Valdostana Veal

ingredients.item: about 8 veal scaloppine, 2 per person (depending on the size of the scaloppine)

method: Flatten the scaloppine by beating them with a meat tenderiser. Put a slice of fontina cheese on each scaloppine and fold the meat over. Secure the scaloppine with a toothpick and thread a fresh sage leaf through the toothpick. Now dust the scaloppine with flour.

Melt the butter with the olive oil, add the garlic and the rest of the sage leaves, then the veal. Fry the scaloppine on all sides, until golden. Now add the dry white wine and continue cooking, turning the scaloppine a few times, until cooked – about 5 minutes. Add salt and pepper to taste. If the sauce looks dry, add a little stock.
Serve immediately while still hot. I like to serve this with Patate Arrosto con Funghi Porcini.

name: Vanilla Almond Date Balls
intro: Vanilla is such a great flavor, and it seems to make something a treat without going over the top. Almond flour and protein powder is added for an extra oomph of protein.

ingredients.item: sunflower seed kernels, ground fine in a small food processor

method: Line an 8-inch square baking dish with parchment paper and come up about 3 inches on opposite sides. This will act as a handle to remove the squares from the dish.

In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium-high heat. Add the sugar and vanilla. Mix the in oats and cook for 2 minutes. Add the hempseed and protein powder and mix well. Transfer half of the mixture into the prepared dish and press firmly and evenly into all edges and corners.

Place the chocolate and peanut butter in a small saucepan. Heat over low heat until chocolate is melted and all is well combined. Pour over the bottom layer in the prepared dish and smooth evenly all over the top. Crumble the remaining oat mixture over the top as evenly as possible and lightly press into the chocolate.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Grab the “handles” of the parchment paper and lift out of the dish. Place on a cutting sheet and slice into sixteen squares.

name: Vanilla Breakfast Smoothie
intro: This smoothie is perfect for an eclectic plant-based breakfast. You need only seven ingredients, and you can make it in less than 10 minutes.

ingredients.item: 15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
ground chia seeds or chia seeds, divided
ground chia seeds or chia seeds
frozen banana, 4 slices reserved for topping
almond milk or other dairy-free milk
plus 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, divided
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and crumbled
Slow Cooker Maple Breakfast Links, sliced thick (page 276)
15-ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed
peeled and sliced apples (I like them kind of thick)
almond milk or other dairy-free milk
Slow Cooker Maple Breakfast Links, sliced (page 276)
15-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
flour tortillas, 8 to 10 inches in diameter

method: Add all the ingredients except for 2 tablespoons of the peanut butter and the sunflower seeds to a large bowl. Mix well. It will seem very wet but the chia seeds and oats will absorb some of the milk. Cover and place in the refrigerator to set overnight.
To serve in the morning, dot the remaining 2 tablespoons peanut butter around the inside of two bowls and fill each with the overnight oats. Garnish with sunflower seeds, if desired.

name: Vanilla Chocolate Chip Cupcakes
servings: makes 12 standard size cupcakes or 24 minis
intro: Occasionally, I crave a vanilla cupcake instead of chocolate, but I still want it well studded with vegan chocolate chips and topped with swirls of rich frosting. Piping the frosting through a pastry bag and sprinkling the cupcakes with more chocolate chips is my idea of pretty and delicious.

ingredients.item: plus 1 tablespoon / 73 grams organic all-purpose flour
/ 70 grams organic whole wheat pastry flour
plus 1 tablespoon / 124 grams organic granulated sugar
mild tasting extra-virgin olive oil or organic neutral vegetable oil
/ 61 grams mini vegan chocolate chips, divided

method: Position a rack in the upper third of oven and preheat to 350°F / 180°C. Line a 12-cup standard cupcake tin with paper liners.
In a small bowl, mix the vinegar and milk. Set aside for 10 minutes to clabber.

Place a wire mesh strainer over a medium bowl. Add the all-purpose flour, pastry flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt to the strainer. Stir with a whisk to sift the ingredients into the bowl. (If any small bits remain in the strainer, add them to the mixture in the bowl.) Whisk to aerate the mixture.
Stir the oil and vanilla into the clabbered milk. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and whisk until the batter is smooth. Stir about half the chocolate chips into the batter.

Divide the batter evenly between the cups, filling each about halfway full. Sprinkle the remaining chocolate chips on top of the batter, dividing evenly between the cups. Bake for 17 to 18 minutes or until a wooden toothpick or skewer inserted into the center comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs.
Cool the tin on a wire rack for 5 minutes. Lift each cake onto the rack and cool completely. Refrigerate until cold before finishing with Creamy Chocolate Cupcake Frosting (page 270).

name: Vanilla Custard Cream Filling
intro: A typical pastry cream, or stirred custard, is made on the stovetop using milk or cream, egg yolks, and starch. Butter may also be an ingredient. Flavorings include vanilla, chocolate, coffee, or liqueurs. A properly made pastry cream is silken and luxurious—and loaded with artery-clogging fat. This recipe, on the other hand, is made in a blender from a base of heart-healthy cashews. Use the custard in the Intensely Chocolate Trifle (page 110), or to fill the Éclairs (page 119). Spread a layer over a ganache-filled cookie crust, or spoon it over fresh fruit. Add a heavy grating of dark chocolate and a cookie and you will have a treat that is rich tasting without the bad fat.

ingredients.item: / 142 grams whole cashews, rinsed and soaked 4 hours to overnight
canned full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, well-stirred (do not use light)
Seeds from 1 2-inch / 5-cm vanilla bean, or increase the vanilla extract to 1 tablespoon / 15 ml

method: Drain the cashews in a strainer. It is important that the cashews are drained well before using. Blend the cashews, coconut milk, sugar, oil, and salt, starting on low and quickly increasing the speed to high for 2 minutes, until the purée is smooth, thick, and warm.

Add the agar powder and guar gum. Blend starting on low, and quickly increase the speed to high. Blend for about 2 minutes, or until the mixture boils; it will actually sputter. If you hear the motor laboring at any point, or if the cream stops moving, use the tamper to push the cream until it starts moving again.
Immediately pour the cream into a container. Stir in the vanilla extract and seeds, if using.
Cool to room temperature, cover, and refrigerate for 4 hours to overnight. The custard will become quite thick as it chills. Stir before using.

Drain the cashews in a strainer. It is important that the cashews are drained well before using. Blend the cashews, coconut milk, sugar, oil, and salt, starting on low and quickly increasing the speed to high. You will need to do this in batches and blend longer, depending on the size of the machine. Add the guar gum and blend for 1 minute.

Pour the cream into a medium (8-inch / 20-cm) skillet. Add the agar powder and cook over medium-low heat, whisking continuously just until the custard boils. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract and seeds, if using.
Pour the cream into a container, cool to room temperature, cover, and refrigerate for 4 hours to overnight. The custard will thicken as it chills. Stir before using.

name: Vanilla custard with roasted strawberries and rhubarb
intro: fridge until ready to assemble. Serve this with some shortbread alongside, if you’re

ingredients.item: oz/200g strawberries, hulled and halved lengthwise
cornstarch rounded ¼ cup/60g granulated sugar

method: Mix the rhubarb and strawberries with the sugar and arrange in a medium ovenproof dish; you want the fruit to  t snugly. Bake for 12–13 minutes, until the fruit has softened but still retains its shape and the sugar has melted.
Don’t worry if there is a tiny amount of sugar that hasn’t melted; just give the fruit a gentle stir and the sugar will dissolve. Set aside to cool.
Decrease the oven temperature to 375°F.

For the custard, place the egg yolks, cornstarch, sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl and whisk until smooth. Gradually pour in the cream and whisk until combined. Pour the custard into a 10-inch/25cm high-sided ovenproof dish.

Place the dish inside a larger ovenproof dish and  ll the larger dish with boiling water so it rises about ½-inch/1cm up the sides. Bake for 25 minutes, until the custard has set and is starting to brown on top. Remove from the oven, set aside to cool, then transfer to the fridge to chill.
Once chilled, spoon half of the fruit and juice on top and serve with the remaining fruit and juice alongside.
Sumac-roasted strawberries with yogurt cream

This is a good dessert if you have overripe strawberries that are slightly past their best. Roasting them makes them deliciously soft and sticky. All of the elements can be made 3 days in advance—keep them separate in the fridge and assemble when ready to serve. Serve this as it is, for a light summer dessert, or with shortbread biscuits. Thanks to Helen Graham.

name: Vanilla Iced Latte
method: Add the espresso, milk, and vanilla to a pitcher.
Mix until combined and pour into a serving glass filled with ice.

name: Vanilla Spice Ice Cream
intro:
MY BUDDY MATT HALTEMAN suggested that I use white beans in this ice cream to give it a creamier consistency. Although I typically recommend cooking beans from scratch, using canned is fine for this recipe; just rinse them well before blending. When I was making final edits to this book, someone gifted me with a copy of Smoke and Pickles, by chef Edward Lee. He includes a recipe for Cornbread-Sorghum Milkshake, which inspired me to create the unbelievably creamy Vanilla Spice Bourbon/Rum Shake, described in the sidebar.

Allspice is one of the most important ingredients in Caribbean cuisine, and it makes this ice cream a delicious and appropriate accompaniment for Cocoa-Spice Cake with Crystallized Ginger and Coconut-Chocolate Ganache. Feel free to modify the basic recipe to come up with your own versions. Change the spices or add fresh fruit and make it your own.

ingredients.item: cooked navy or cannellini beans, drained

method: Put the beans and coconut milk in a blender and process until creamy. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a medium saucepan. Stir in the sugar, molasses, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt. Cut the vanilla bean in half lengthwise. Scrape the seeds into the saucepan, then throw in the pod. Cook over medium heat, whisking occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is gently simmering, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in the cashew cream. Remove from the heat and let cool completely. Transfer to a medium bowl, cover, and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 6 hours or overnight.

Remove the vanilla pod, pour the mixture into an ice cream maker, and freeze according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Transfer to an airtight container and freeze until firm, about 8 hours or overnight.
tips: To make one serving, put ½ cup Vanilla Spice Ice Cream in a blender. Add ¼ cup Date-Sweetened Almond Milk and 1 tablespoon of bourbon or rum (or to taste) and pulse until thick and creamy. (Pictured here.)

name: Vatana Gajar Handvo
intro: This is the best savoury cake you’ll ever eat. Handvo is a Gujarati-style snack that is cooked in a regular pan on the stove instead of an oven. It cuts like a cake and, conventionally, dairy yoghurt is its most essential ingredient. However, even with store-bought or home-made almond yoghurt, the recipe turns out just as beautiful.
method: Wash the rice, split green gram, pigeon peas, split black gram and Bengal gram thoroughly. Combine them in a bowl and add just enough water to cover. Let the mixture soak for 4 hours.
Drain and grind the mixture into a smooth paste. Add almond yoghurt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger–chilli paste, carrot and green peas and season it with salt.

In a deep skillet, heat 1 tbsp oil and add 1 pinch mustard seeds, ½ tsp sesame seeds and 2-3 curry leaves. Once the tempering begins to crackle, pour 3-4 ladles of the handvo batter until it begins to resemble a thick cake.
Cover and cook the batter on medium heat for 8-9 minutes.
Flip and cook it on the other side for 4-5 minutes. Repeat the process until you have exhausted all your batter.
Serve hot with mint–coriander chutney.

name: Veal with Tuna Mayonnaise

ingredients.item: veal nut (noix or topside), wrapped very tightly in cheesecloth (muslin)
arge carrots, cut into large pieces
celery stalks, cut into large pieces
arge onion, cut into large pieces
handful capers, plus extra for garnish

method: Choose a saucepan that the veal will just fit into. Place the veal in the pan and cover with cold water. Add the wine, carrots, celery, onion, bay leaves and peppercorns. Put the lid on. Bring to the boil and then reduce the heat to low. Let it simmer for 20–25 minutes. Allow the meat to cool in the stock (see Note).

For the mayonnaise, beat the egg yolks with the salt and mustard then, while continuing to beat steadily, add the oil drop by drop – as the yolks begin to thicken, increase the oil to a steady trickle. Add some lemon juice then more oil, alternating until you have used up both the oil and lemon juice. Season to taste.
Place the tuna, anchovies and capers in a food processor, pulse to mix and add 1–2 ladlefuls of the veal stock. The tuna mixture should be like a thick cream. Taste and add salt and pepper if needed.

Slice the veal very thinly and arrange on a serving plate. Mix some of the mayonnaise with the tuna mixture and spread some of it over the sliced meat and put the rest in a bowl, to serve on the side. Garnish with capers.
The left-over stock from cooking the veal can be used to make risotto. It can also be frozen for later use.

name: Vegan Bbq ‘ribs’
method: Heat the oven to 350 degrees.
Mix the wet ingredients (water, tahini, tamari & liquid smoke) in a small bowl. Set aside.
In a larger bowl – mix the dry ingredients (wheat gluten & spices) and add the wet ingredients. Mix it up until that gooey hamburger-looking stuff comes together
Grease a loaf pan & press the seitan into the pan. Smooth it flat. Bake at 350 for about 30 minutes. Remove from oven & transfer the seitan to a plate & slather it with BBQ sauce
Put the seitan, BBQ sauce side down, onto the grill. Slather lots more BBQ sauce on the other side. Now just cook this until it looks the way you would want ribs to look.

name: Vegan Bibimbap

ingredients.item: g / 7 oz firm non-GMO (cotton not silken) tofu, pressed
soy sauce or tamari for GF version)
Gochujang (Korean chilli paste) this is the one I used
g / 3½ oz mushrooms (shiitake if you can get them)
ml / ¼ cup rice wine vinegar + 60-120 ml / ¼-½ cup water
soy sauce or tamari for GF version)
maple syrup (or sugar dissolved in soy sauce)

method: Cut a pressed block of tofu into equal size cubes – I got 12 out of mine.

Place the tofu in a shallow bowl and pour soy sauce (mixed in with 1 tsp of Gochujang) over it. Set the tofu aside for at least 30 minutes to allow the tofu to absorb the marinade, making sure you turn the pieces to the other side at least once, halfway through.

If you have a non-stick pan, you can pan-fry the tofu. Heat up 2 tsp of oil on a non-stick pan. Place the marinated tofu cubes into the hot oil. Fry, turning frequently until browned on all sides. Be careful as the tofu is likely to splatter a little bit initially.

If you don’t have a non-stick pan or want to reduce the amount of oil you consume, you can also bake the tofu. Set the oven to 180° C / 355° F and place the marinated cubes of tofu on a baking sheet. Bake for about 25-30 minutes, turning once, halfway through.
PICKLED DAIKON (make a day in advance if you can)
Slice the daikon into thin slices and place in a jar.
Bring rice vinegar, water (60-120 ml / ¼-½ cup, depending how sharp you like your pickles), sugar and salt to a gentle boil.

Pour the hot pickling liquid over the daikon. The pickles can be eaten straight away, but they are worth making a day in advance as their flavour develops with time. Store in an airtight jar in the fridge.
Whisk all of the dressing ingredients together in a medium size bowl.

Heat up 2 tsp of oil in a medium non-stick pan. Throw in the mushrooms and fry them gently until they are nicely browned on all sides. Season with salt and pepper once fried so that the mushrooms don’t release too much water during frying.

Remove the mushrooms from the pan, throw in the spinach and a splash of water. Cook on a low heat, stirring from time to time, until the spinach wilts and most of the excess water cooks out. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide all the veggies and cooked tofu between two bowls. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and top with the Gochujang dressing.

name: Vegan Birria Tacos
method: Cook the mushrooms in the olive oil.
Add onions into it and cook until soft and translucent.
Next, add the garlic, and dried chilies into the mixture.
Add the taco seasoning into the mixture and cook for five minutes.
Heat the taco shells in an oven.
Fill the taco sheets with the above mixture.
Add the creamy red sauce, and cilantro leaves on top.
Your dish is ready to be served.

name: Vegan Chicharrón Sin Carne
intro: This vegan chicharrón sin carne (meaning “fried without meat”) is my take on a popular Hispanic dish called chicharrón de pollo, which is chicken chunks that are breaded and seasoned, then fried. The “meat” in this dish is jackfruit, marinated and coated with herbs and spices. Once fried, it is topped with lime juice for that signature flavor. Chicharrón is popularly served with tostones, which are green plantains that are fried, then smashed, then fried again. I use jackfruit for this dish because it can mimic pork or chicken and is perfect to manipulate.
method: In a large pot, boil the jackfruit for 1 hour to extract the brine. After an hour, drain and squeeze out the excess water with a paper towel. In a bowl, combine the boiled jackfruit and mojo sauce, then marinate overnight in the fridge.
Get two medium-sized bowls, one for mixing the dry batter and one for the wet. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
For the dry batter, in one bowl, combine 3 cups (375 g) of the flour with the Sazón, adobo, oregano, garlic powder, onion powder and salt to taste.

For the wet batter, in the other bowl, combine the remaining 2 cups (250 g) of flour, nondairy milk, hot sauce and vinegar, and mix. This batter shouldn’t be too thick or too loose. Add more flour or milk accordingly.
In a baking pan, lay down the jackfruit and separate them a bit, then bake for 20 minutes. This is to dehydrate the jackfruit a bit to make it meatier.

In a large pot, heat your oil to 370°F (190°C). Using one hand, dip your jackfruit into the wet batter; then, with your other hand, coat the jackfruit with dry batter. If you want a supercrispy crunch, double batter the jackfruit. Repeat until all the jackfruit has been coated.
Fry the jackfruit on both sides for about 6 minutes, or until golden brown. Remove from the oil and let rest on a cooling rack. Squeeze the lime juice on the jackfruit chicharrones.

name: Vegan Chicken Salad

ingredients.item: Vietnamese mint, stems removed and roughly chopped
makrut lime leaves, cut into fine threads

method: In a medium skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil over low heat. When hot, add seitan and cook until golden brown on all sides (3 to 5 minutes). Remove and place on a paper towel–lined plate to drain and let cool.
Tear seitan into thin strips along fiber grain, place in a medium bowl, and set aside.
In a medium skillet, heat remaining 3 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium heat. When hot, add leek and cook and stir until golden brown (1 to 2 minutes). Remove from heat and let cool.
In a small bowl, combine sugar, lime juice, soy sauce, salt, and stock powder (if using). Stir well until all solids are dissolved.
Pour half of the dressing into the bowl of shredded seitan and mix well so seitan will absorb it.
Add fried leek, pepper, Vietnamese mint, lime leaves, and the rest of the dressing. Mix well and serve immediately.

name: Vegan Crab Noodle Soup

ingredients.item: block (14 ounces/400 g) firm tofu, mashed
vegetable or mushroom stock powder, plus more to taste
firm tofu, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
fresh mushrooms (straw, beech, or king oyster), stems trimmed and sliced
vegetable or mushroom stock powder, plus more if needed
tamarind paste or 1 teaspoon tamarind concentrate mixed with 2 teaspoons water
leaf or iceberg lettuce, leaves torn into small pieces or shredded, for serving
lime, cut into wedges, for serving

method: RIÊU In a medium bowl, combine mashed tofu, 1 tablespoon of sugar, 1 teaspoon of stock powder, and 2 teaspoons of the annatto oil, and mix well.

Heat the remaining 2 teaspoons annatto oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. When hot, add tofu mixture, stir, and cook until tofu absorbs all seasoning (about 3 minutes). Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Heat ½ cup (120 ml) of the vegetable oil in a medium nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add tofu cubes and cook until golden brown on all sides (10 to 15 minutes). Transfer to a cooling rack or paper towel–lined plate to drain.

In a medium stockpot, heat remaining ½ cup (120 ml) vegetable oil over medium-low heat. When hot, add leek and cook and stir until fragrant (about 1 minute). Add tomatoes and mushrooms, stir, and cook until soft (about 3 minutes). Add vegetable broth, salt, and stock powder.
Add tamarind paste, deep-fried tofu, and 1 tablespoon of sugar and bring to a boil. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes. Season to taste with more salt and/or stock powder if needed.
If using, place chao and fermented soybean sauce in a food processor or blender and process with the water until smooth. (You can also mash by hand with a spoon.) Stir mixture into broth.
Follow the instructions on the package to cook the dried rice vermicelli noodles.

Divide the cooked noodles into serving bowls, spoon the riêu on top, and then ladle the hot broth over the top. Serve with a platter of shredded lettuce and perilla leaves with lime wedges on the side.

name: Vegan Crab Soup

ingredients.item: firm tofu, finely crumbled with a fork
silken tofu, finely crumbled with a fork
vegetable or mushroom stock powder, divided
cube store-bought or homemade chao, finely crushed
minced enoki mushrooms, stems trimmed and rinsed with salted water
sawtooth herb or cilantro, finely chopped, for garnish

method: In a large bowl, combine both types of tofu, 1 teaspoon of the stock powder, salt, sugar, chao, fermented soybean sauce, annatto oil, and pepper, and mix well. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes to allow the flavor to develop.

In a medium skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil over low heat. When hot, add leek and cook and stir until fragrant (about 1 minute). Add the tofu mixture and flatten its surface with a spatula. Cook on low until the mixture is set (2 to 3 more minutes), and then remove from heat.
In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil over medium heat. Add tomatoes and cook and stir until soft (about 3 minutes). Add water and bring to a boil.

Add mushrooms and the remaining 1 teaspoon stock powder, taste, and add more salt if needed. Cook over medium heat until tomatoes are broken down and mushrooms are soft (about 2 more minutes), and then remove from heat.
Transfer to a large serving bowl or divide into smaller serving bowls.
Add the tofu mixture (riêu) to the hot soup, garnish with sawtooth herb or cilantro, and serve hot.

name: Vegan Cream
intro: I always have a box full of vegan cream in my refrigerator. This cream can be used the same way real dairy cream is used. Eat it with fruit or add a dollop to breakfast porridge, or use it to make dal makhani and other full-bodied Indian gravies.
method: In a bowl, soak cashew nuts for 5 hours.
Drain and transfer the nuts into a blender.
Add just enough water to the blender to allow the nuts to turn. Blend at high speed.
Once the mixture becomes creamy, blend it for 30 seconds.
Store the cream in a jar for up to 2 days in the refrigerator.

name: Vegan Dried Fish and Bitter Melon Salad
intro: In gỏi khổ qua cá chay, dried bean curd replaces the dried fish. You can use karela (Indian bitter melon) or Chinese bitter melon for this recipe. Karela has a darker-green skin and tighter, more pronounced bumps while the Chinese melon is lighter green and has wider, shallower bumps. To help reduce the bitterness of the melon, see step 4.

ingredients.item: large or 2 small karela or Chinese bitter melons, seeds removed and thinly sliced
round leaf mint or mint, roughly chopped if leaves are large

method: In a medium bowl, mash the chao cubes with a spoon until it’s a smooth paste. Add sugar and stock powder, and mix well. Add flour and stir briskly until you get a thick, smooth, homogenous mixture.
Spread a thin layer of the mixture on each dried bean curd stick.

Fill the bottom of a saucepan with about 2 inches (5 cm) of oil and place over medium heat. Check with a cooking thermometer and when oil reaches 320°F (160°C), add dried bean curd sticks and deep-fry until crisp and golden brown (1 to 2 minutes). Remove fried bean curd sticks, drain excess oil, and then cut into small pieces (about 2-inches/5-cm long).
Scrape all seeds and white spongy part off melons, slice them thinly crosswise, and then rinse a few times. (Optional: To reduce the bitterness, you can blanch the slices, and then drain.)
Toss bitter melons, carrots, and salt in a large bowl, and let sit for 15 minutes.
Rinse, squeeze out excess water, and then place in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, sugar, and lime juice, and stir well until sugar is dissolved.
Add the dressing to the bowl with the salad mixture and toss well.
Add mint, cilantro, dried fish, pickled scallion heads (if using), and roasted peanuts, and mix together.
Serve with sesame rice crackers (if using).

name: Vegan Fish Dipping Sauce
method: In a small bowl, combine vegan fish sauce, sugar, water, and lime juice, and stir well until sugar is completely dissolved.
Add garlic and chili pepper to float on top.

name: Vegan Fish Sauce

ingredients.item: sheet (4 by 8 inches/10 by 20 cm) dried kelp (kombu seaweed)

method: In a medium saucepan, combine dried shiitake mushrooms, dried kelp, and water, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Boil for 5 minutes, and then add pineapple, salt, rock sugar, cinnamon, star anise, and soy sauce.
Simmer on low heat until the sauce is reduced by half, about 30 minutes.
Strain to remove all solids, let cool, and then transfer to an airtight glass jar or bottle.
Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

name: Vegan Haleem
intro: One of the rare dishes in this book that tries to vegan-ize a hardcore meat dish, my vegan haleem is a hearty bowl that is ideal for a winter night’s dinner. It’s got whole grains, vegetables and a generous helping of birista, of which I cannot get enough.

ingredients.item: mixed vegetables (cauliflower, peas, carrots, French beans) (diced)

method: Boil the wholewheat grains with a pinch of salt until tender. Drain and keep aside.
In a heavy-bottomed vessel, heat the oil and add the cumin seeds to it. Once they begin to crackle, add the ginger–garlic paste and green chilli. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add the onion and continue sautéing until it becomes golden brown.
Add the coriander powder, red chilli powder and turmeric powder. Cook for 2-3 minutes on medium flame.

Add the wholewheat grains and lentils and enough water to cover the ingredients. Allow this to cook on low flame for 40–45 minutes. Once it is done, take it off the heat and grind it into a coarse paste using a hand-blender.
Place the vessel back on the stove and add the vegetables to it. Allow this to simmer for 20 minutes on medium flame. If the haleem seems too dry, add a cup of warm water to it.
Finish with garam masala and salt. Stir well.
Garnish the haleem with mint leaves, coriander leaves, lemon juice and birista. Serve hot.

name: Vegan King Calamari
intro: Calamari was often my go-to item at brunch to share at the table with friends. If you don’t know what calamari is, it is squid cut into circles, battered and then deep-fried, usually paired with marinara sauce or aioli. My vegan version is made using king oyster mushrooms. This mushroom makes a great replacement because it can be cut up like the calamari and resembles its chewy texture. The seasoned batter makes it salty and crispy.
method: Remove the caps of the king oyster mushrooms and set them aside. Using an apple corer, remove the center of each of the mushroom stems. Then, slice the coreless mushrooms to get ring-shaped pieces. Slice the mushroom caps to get extra slices.

In a medium-sized bowl, combine the nondairy milk, 1 cup (125 g) of the flour, 1 tablespoon (9 g) of the garlic powder and the hot sauce. Use a whisk to mix everything together until smooth. This is your wet batter.
In a separate bowl, combine the remaining flour, nori furikake, remaining tablespoon (9 g) of garlic powder, Old Bay Seasoning, salt and pepper. Whisk to mix everything together until smooth.

Dip a batch of the mushroom pieces into the wet batter and let the mushrooms soak for about 5 minutes. Then, using a skimmer, scoop out the mushrooms (making sure to shake off any excess liquid) and add them to the Old Bay mixture to seal the breading.

Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot or a deep fryer to 375°F (190°C). Use the skimmer to scoop the breaded mushrooms and add them in batches to the hot oil. Let them fry for 3 to 5 minutes, making sure to stir the mushrooms from time to time so they don’t stick together.
Remove the mushrooms once they are golden brown and place them on a paper towel–covered plate to absorb some of the excess oil.
In a small bowl, stir together the vegan mayonnaise and sriracha to serve with the hot calamari. Alternatively, you can serve them with marinara sauce and a bit of lemon for zest.

name: Vegan Mexican Chocolate Cake
method: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Grease a cake pan.
Take a bowl, and combine sugar, flour, cocoa, cinnamon, baking
soda, and cayenne.
Mix vanilla, oil, vinegar, and water.
Put the mixture in the cake pan, then bake for almost 30 minutes.
Sprinkle powdered sugar, and serve.

name: Vegan Omelette with Boiled Plantain
intro: Plantain for breakfast is very common in Nigeria and if it isn’t served with a stew, it is served with eggs. Here we will make a bean-based vegan omelette that’s bursting with fresh and flavourful vegetables.

ingredients.item: ripe yellow plantains 1/2 cup beans flour 1/2 cup water
1/2 teaspoon salt (or black salt/kala namak for an eggy flavour) Sunflower oil for frying

method: Cut the tops and tails of the plantains and use a knife to score the skin all the way down the side. Leave the skin on and cut each plantain into 3-4 large chunks. Place them in a pot and cover completely with water. Bring to a boil then cook on medium heat for 20 minutes until tender. Drain the excess water, leave the plantains to cool for a few minutes then peel and discard the skins.
To make the vegan omelette, combine the beans flour, water, chopped onions, peppers, chilli, sweetcorn and salt in a bowl. Mix well and set aside for 10 minutes.

Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small non-stick frying pan and pour in half of the omelette batter. Gently spread it around the bottom of the pan with the back of a spoon to form a round omelette, cover and cook for 5 minutes over medium-high heat. Use a spatula to loosen the sides and gently flip the omelette over to cook on the other side for a further 2-3 minutes. Gently fold the omelette in half and transfer to a plate. Repeat this process with the rest of the batter to make another omelette. The omelette will appear stiﬀ at first but will soften as it starts to cool.

name: Vegan Orange Blossom Honey
intro: If you don’t eat honey for ethical reasons or because you find it congesting, as I do, this orange-scented honey substitute is a superb alternative. I make a double recipe in a large saucepan so I always have a jar in my refrigerator for drizzling on nondairy yogurt, over puddings, on bread, and for dipping apples during the Rosh Hashanah holiday.

ingredients.item: brown rice syrup, warmed in the jar until liquid (see page 23)
pure maple syrup, Grade B or dark amber
Strips of zest from ½ of a medium organic orange

method: Combine the rice, agave, and maple syrups and the sugar in a medium saucepan with high sides and cook over medium heat to a boil. Add the orange zest.
Lower the heat and cook for 10 minutes, stirring a few times and adjusting the heat as necessary to maintain a low boil.

Remove the saucepan from the heat. Test the final consistency: Spoon a scant tablespoon into a small dish and refrigerate for 10 minutes. If the honey is thick enough, cool to room temperature in the saucepan. If not, cook it another few minutes.
Pour the syrup through a fine mesh strainer into a jar. Cover and refrigerate for up to 1 month.

name: Vegan Puerto Rican Pastelón
intro: Pastelón is a popular Puerto Rican dish made using sweet plantains, ground meat and mozzarella cheese. Think: lasagna, but much sweeter and more comforting. My family didn’t make this much, but I had it for the first time at my friend Melissa’s house during high school. Melissa and I had class together and worked in a neighborhood supermarket called Pioneer in Morris Park. Melissa and her family are from the Dominican Republic, and for dinner one day, they offered me pastelón. At the time, I had no idea what it was. Melissa explained it was made with sweet plantains and raisins. Although I thought it was good, the raisins made it too sweet for me. (I’m very much a savory girl.) I decided to make it without the raisins and loved how it turned out. The sweet plantains meshed into the savory meat (which I replace with walnuts and shiitake mushrooms), and the melted cheese between the layers makes it such a comforting treat. Keep in mind when picking the sweet plantain, the darker, the sweeter—just make sure it isn’t mushy.

ingredients.item: bags shredded vegan mozzarella cheese (I recommend Violife® brand)

method: Slice your yellow plantains the long way, into three or four thin slices per plantain, depending on how thick it is.

In a large, deep pot, heat your oil to 350°F (180°C). Working in batches, add about six slices of plantain and fry until fully cooked through. Transfer to a paper towel to drain. Repeat until all your plantains are fried.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a medium bowl, stir together the tomato sauce and picadillo.

In an 8 x 8–inch (20 x 20–cm) baking dish, arrange a layer of fried plantain on the bottom, then layer with half of the picadillo mixture. Sprinkle one-third of the vegan mozzarella cheese on top. Follow this with two more layers, but do not put the picadillo mixture on the very top layer. Instead, add only the remaining cheese and pour the JUST Egg over the top of the pastelón and along the edges, to prevent the pastelón from drying out during baking, and for binding.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then remove the foil and broil for an additional 6 to 7 minutes. Cut into eight slices and serve with white rice or by itself. ¡Buen provecho!

name: Vegan Shroom Shrimp
intro: Yes, vegan shroom shrimp. Made using mushrooms. I wanted to stick to a natural, plant-based approach when making a vegan alternative to shrimp. Using king oyster mushrooms are perfect because you can shape them into shrimp, and after they are cooked, they have the same plump texture. This vegan shrimp is chewy, savory and has that perfect seafood taste. Boiling the mushrooms in a flavored broth is going to allow flavors to immerse into the mushrooms before cooking, making them even tastier.
method: Wash and cut off the caps and woody ends of the king oyster mushrooms, leaving the body.

Using a small, sharp knife, carve out a small, acute-shaped triangle from the top to the bottom of the body of each mushrooms. The triangle should be cut from a quarter of the shroom at one corner. You can now slice ½-inch (1.3-cm) rounds of the mushrooms, resembling the shape of a shrimp.

In a large pot, combine your vegetable stock, nori furikake and salt and bring to a boil, then add the shrooms. Boil the shrooms for about 15 minutes, then remove them from the water and squeeze out any excess liquid using dry paper towels.
Season with Old Bay and enjoy as is, or add them to your favorite recipes, such as the shrimp stew in Mofonguitos con Vegan Camarones.

name: Vegan Street Tacos
method: Cook the quinoa in the vegetable broth.
Add tomato paste, onion, green bell pepper, cumin and chili powder
into it.
Next, add the mushrooms into it and when done remove from the
stove.
Place the mixture on the corn tortillas; add the walnuts, tamari sauce
on top.
Garnish with cilantro leaves.
Your dish is ready to be served.

name: Vegan Thai Green Curry
intro: A vegetarian curry that will satisfy even the most die-hard meat eaters. Rich in umami and vegetables, which are chosen for its chewy, satisfying texture. Not forgetting the secret ingredient that adds firmness and bright color to store-bought curry. For a gluten-free curry, add gluten-free soy sauce.
method: To make the curry paste, place the leafy greens, curry paste, miso, and mushroom into a blender and well.
Heat ¾ cup of coconut milk over medium heat in a heavy-bottomed pot for about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium and add curry paste (Step 1). Stir for 3-5 minutes.
Add remaining coconut milk and water and let it boil.
Add fried tofu, bamboo shoots, winter melon, palm sugar and soy sauce.
Shred the makrut lime leaves, then add them into the pot. Simmer the curry for about 9 minutes
Add the red peppers and let it boil for 1 more minute. When done, turn off the stove, stir in the fresh basil and let it wilt in the curry.
Serve with jasmine rice immediately, or later (like most Thai curries, it tastes even better the next day!)

name: Vegetable Bhaji
servings: serves 4 or more as part of a multi-course meal
intro:
Any seasonal vegetables can be used for this recipe. I’ve recommended a few, but feel free to add whatever you like. Vegetable bhaji is essentially a stir-fry with a little base curry sauce and spices mixed in. Be careful not to overcook the vegetables in the sauce. They need to have a bit of bite to them.

Consider this a slightly fancier version of the pre-cooked onions and vegetables. Vegetable bhaji can be served as a curry on its own, or you could mix a few spoonfuls into the curry of your choice.

time.prep: 10 MINS, PLUS MAKING THE BASE CURRY SAUCE
time.total: 10 MINS, PLUS MAKING THE BASE CURRY SAUCE10 MINS

ingredients.item: yellow and 1 red (bell) pepper, thinly sliced
green bird’s eye chillies, finely chopped
small carrot, peeled and thinly sliced
base curry sauce (see quick and easy base curry sauce), heated
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

method: Heat the oil in a large wok or frying pan over a high heat. When hot, throw in the mustard seeds. When they begin to crackle (after about 30 seconds), reduce the heat to medium–high, then add the curry leaves and stir to combine.

Now add the sliced onions and yellow and red (bell) peppers and fry for about 5 minutes until the onions are translucent and soft. Add the garlic and ginger paste, chillies, turmeric and mixed powder, followed by the tomato purée. Let these sizzle for 1 minute, then stir in the rest of the vegetables to fry for about 2 minutes, stirring continuously.
Pour in the base curry sauce and simmer undisturbed, stirring only if it is catching on the pan.
When the vegetables are cooked to your liking, add the tomato wedges and dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Season with salt and black pepper and sprinkle with the garam masala to serve.
tips: A couple of pre-cooked potatoes and a little of the cooking sauce is a nice addition.

name: Vegetable Curry Couscous
intro: A variety of veggies make this interesting side dish versatile. You can serve chicken in an apple, onion, and curry sauce over the top and sprinkle it with flaked coconut. It can also be made with quinoa; just adjust the cooking time.

ingredients.item: small leek, cleaned and thinly sliced
salt and ground black pepper to taste

method: Place vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat, cook, and stir the onion, leek, celery, red bell pepper, and garlic until the onion is translucent for about 5 minutes.

Pour in the chicken stock, bring to a boil, and stir in the carrot, tomatoes, couscous, raisins, and currants. Season with curry powder, turmeric, salt, and black pepper; bring the mixture back to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and allow to cook for 5 minutes .
Remove from heat. Let the couscous stand covered for 5 minutes, and fluff with a fork. Sprinkle with sliced almonds.

name: Vegetable Jumble with Thai Seitan
intro: Here’s an eclectic mix of all the best and most popular vegetables. A tasty seitan is added, and all of the spices make this jumble pop with flavor.

ingredients.item: small head cauliflower, cut into florets
small head broccoli, cut into florets
cooked black beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, chopped small, and 1 tablespoon adobo sauce
raw cashews, soaked from 1 hour to overnight and drained
Steamed Seitan Chipotle Links, torn into bite-size pieces (page 284)
15-ounce can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cut into ½-inch cubes
Slow Cooker Versatile Seitan Balls, chopped (page 279)
Slow Cooker Versatile Seitan Balls, cubed (page 279)
15-ounce cans black beans, drained and rinsed
chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, finely chopped
Additional toppings, such as more salsa, avocado or guacamole, and black olives
whole wheat or sprouted grain tortillas
Steamed Seitan Smoky Nuggets (page 283), cut into bite-size pieces if necessary
broccoli, stems peeled and diced, florets cut into bite-size pieces
cobs of corn, kernels cut from the cob
hot sauce, such as Tabasco (omit if you don’t like spicy; you can put it on the table instead)
extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed (page 17), and cubed
15-ounce cans black beans, drained and rinsed

method: Add water to a medium saucepan with a steamer insert and bring to a boil. Add the carrots and cauliflower to the insert and steam over boiling water for 5 minutes.
Add the broccoli on top of the cauliflower and steam for 10 more minutes. Poke all the vegetables and make sure they can be easily pierced with a fork. Do not overcook. Al dente is best.

Heat the oil in a large skillet. Add the onion and bell pepper and sauté for 10 minutes. Add the mushrooms to the skillet and cook for 10 more minutes. Add the seitan nuggets and all of the herbs and spices. Stir and heat through for about 2 minutes. Add the cauliflower mixture, stir well, and cook another 5 minutes.

name: Vegetable Pakoras
servings: serves 4 or more as part of a multi-course meal
intro: Vegetable pakoras can be made in lots of ways with many different variations. In fact, if you have tried the onion bhaji recipe opposite, it can be made into vegetable pakoras too. Simply follow that recipe and add a few chopped vegetables of choice and voilà… you’ve got vegetable pakoras! Below is a recipe that is completely different to that one but just as delicious. If you want to make this recipe gluten-free, just leave out the panko breadcrumbs.

ingredients.item: green (bell) pepper, thinly sliced and cut into 2.5cm (1in) pieces
A generous handful of cabbage, shredded (about 90g/1 cup)
shredded baby spinach leaves, large stems removed
gram (chickpea) flour, plus extra if needed

method: Place the vegetables in a large mixing bowl and add the coriander (cilantro).

Sift the gram flour, rice flour, turmeric, salt and Kashmiri chilli powder into a separate bowl and add the lemon juice (if using). Begin slowly pouring about 125ml (½ cup) of water into the flour mixture while whisking until it is about the same consistency as whisked natural yoghurt.
Tip the vegetables into the batter and mix well. Sprinkle the panko breadcrumbs (if using) onto a plate.

Using your hands, form the battered vegetables into balls slightly larger than golf balls and dip them in the panko breadcrumbs. If you are finding the mixture too wet to work with, sift in a little more gram flour. If too dry, add a drop more water.

Heat about 10cm (4in) of oil in a large saucepan or wok to 180°C (355°F). If you don’t have an oil thermometer, the oil is ready when a small piece of the battered vegetables sizzles immediately and rises to the top. You might need to cook the pakoras in batches. Fry until they are crispy, brown and cooked through. This will take about 4 minutes. Serve hot with pakora sauce.
tips: In this recipe I give measurements in both grams and US cups but there’s no need to go rifling through your cupboards for your kitchen scales or cup measures! This isn’t that kind of cooking. Just use any tea cup and adjust, adding more or less of the vegetables should you wish to do so.
